book_title:
The Book of Proverbs,
which the Hebrews call Misle. משלי

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF THE PROVERBS.
intros.text: The firſt booke called Prouerbes, that is, common & vſual pithie ſentences, shorte in wordes, ample in [1] ſenſe; and Parables, ſignifying likenes or ſimilitudes, wherby more important thinges are vnderſtood then expreſſed; inſtructeth and exhorteth new beginners, to lerne, and practiſe al ſortes of vertues, the only right way to true Wiſdome and eternal happines. It may be diuided [2] into foure partes. In the firſt nine chapters the auctor interpoſing certaine general preceptes, [3] produceth wiſdom herſelf inuiting al men to ſeeke her, for the ſpiritual profite, they shal therby enioy. From thence to the 25. chap. he giveth ſundrie more particular precepts, as wel for embracing vertues, as shunning of vices. In the next fiue chapters, more like precepts of the ſame auctor, are added by the care of King Ezechias. In the thirtieth chapter, either another Author, or rather the ſame vnder another title, and in prophetical ſtyle, uttereth like divine ſentences; adding in the laſt chapter, other excellent precepts receiued of his mother: Wherto he adioyneth the praiſe of a right wiſe woman; prophetically the Catholique Church.

notes.text: VVhy this booke is called Prouerbes and Parables.

intros.title: THE THIRD PART OF THE OLD TESTAMENT CONTAINING SAPIENTIAL BOOKS.
intros.text: The argument of Sapiential Books. Hitherto the Law and Hiſtory of God's peculiar people are ſet forth in the former parts of the holie Bible: after which folowed the Booke of pſalms, which in maner of ſtyle, being all in verſe, is a diſtinct part, but in ſubſtance of matter, is an Epitome or brief Summe of all holie Scripture: moſt conveniently therefore placed in the midſt of the reſt, as the Sunne amongſt other Planets, a shining great light in a large houſe. Now enſueth the third part, containing Diuine Inſtructions, or [1] Rules of good life. A doctrine moſt agreeable to God's high wiſdom, and moſt fitly commended to Man, his reaſonable creature in earth. But beſides the principal ſubject, as before is noted (that each part participated with others in their proper contents) ſo here be mani precepts of [2] [3] the Law renewed, ſundry examples of men, and things paſt repeated, and diverſe prophecies uttered of things to come: though in this part more ſpecially is shewed the ground, and as it were, the very life or ſoul of the Law. Which is Reaſon, the true Rule or Directory wherein all good laws are grounded. For it both sheweth what ought to be done, or avoided, & directeth man's judgment to embrace that is good, and to fly from all evil: not only illuminating the underſtanding to ſee that is right and juſt, but alſo diſpoſing the internal affection to deſire, love, chooſe, and preferre the right path of God's law, before whatſoever otherwiſe ſeemeth pleaſant or profitable: & ſo, not withſtanding all dangers, difficulties, diſtreſſes, worldly calamities, and death itſelf, effectually perſuading to perſevere to the end in holie converſation. All which by a general name is called Wiſdom: ◦ compriſing in one word, all good deſires, holy virtues, ſupernal gifts, godly endeavours, and the whole means whereby God is rightly known, & duly ſerued, whereof theſe five Books, teaching this moſt excellent and moſt neceſſary maner of life, are called Sapiential. Nevertheleſs four of them haue alſo other particular names, as appeareth in their titles. Only the fourth is called the Booke of Wiſdom, by appropriation of the general name. All fiue are Canonical and aſſured holie Scripture: as is shewed before, and may be further [4] [5] proved of the two later, which Proteſtants denie. It is alſo evident that King Salomon was [6] Author of the three former: as S. Jerome, S. Auguſtin, and other Fathers prove by the holie text [7] itſelf. It is likewiſe certain that he either writ, or at leaſt by divine inſpiration vttered, much more than is now extant. For the holy Scripture (3. Reg. 4.) teſtifieth that he ſpake three thouſand [8] Parables: and his Songs were a thouſand and five. He diſputed of the trees from the cedar that is in Libanus, unto the hyſſop which cometh out of the wal: and he diſcourſed of beaſts, and fowls, and creeping worms, and fishes. Joſephus (li. 8. c. 2. Antiq.) folowing ſome other Edition, ſaith his ſongs were five thouſand, and parables (as the ordinarie text hath) three thouſand. For he deduced a parable (ſaith Joſephus) throughout every kinde of trees, from the hyſſop to the cedar. In the ſame maner he treated of beaſts, and other living creatures of the earth, water, and ayre. For he was not ignorant of any natural thing, neither omitted to treate thereof, but clearly explicated all their natural properties. Moſt briefly S. Jerome declareth both the Author and matter of theſe [9] three books, ſaying: Salomon the peaceable, and amiable of our Lord correcteth maners: [10] [11] teacheth the nature (of creatures) ioyneth the Church and Chriſt; and ſingeth the ſwete [12] [13] bridal ſong of the holie Mariage.

notes.text: The coherence of this part with the reſt.
Salomon is author of the three firſt.
S. Iero. in proe. S. Aug. li. 17. c. 20. civi.
Other books of Salomon not extant.
A brief ſum of theſe three.

verses.text: THE Parables of Salomon, the ſonne of Dauid, king of Iſrael.
<na>(a)</na> To know wiſdom, and diſcipline:

notes.label: a
notes.text: By theſe ſentencious ſimilitudes the ſtudious may better conceiue and vnderſtand true vviſdom, and the vertues belonging therto.

verses.text: to vnderſtand the wordes of prudence: and to receiue inſtruction of doctrine, iuſtice, and iudgement, and equitie:
that <na>(b)</na> subtilitie may be geuen to litle ones, knowlege and vnderſtanding to the youngman.
The <na>(c)</na> wiſe man hearing shal be wiser: and he that vnderſtandeth, <na>(d)</na> shal poſſeſſe gouernementes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Not only yongmen and inexperienced but alſo the vviſe may lerne more vviſdom by theſe parables.

notes.label: d
notes.text: shal be fitte to gouerne others.

verses.text: He shal vnderſtand a parable, and interpretation, the wordes of the wiſe, and their darke ſayings.
The <na>(e)</na> feare of our Lord is the begynning of wiſdom. Fooles deſpiſe wiſedom and doctrine.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Feare of our Lord, that iſ, reuerence of his diuine Maieſtie with deſire duly to ſerue him, and neuer to offend him, is the firſt degree in aſcending to perfect vviſdom : vvhich conſiſteth not only in the vnderſtanding but alſo in action.

verses.text: My ſonne, <na>(f)</na> heare the diſcipline of thy father, and leaue not the lawe of thy mother:

notes.label: f
notes.text: The firſt precept is to lerne of our elders.

verses.text: that grace may be added to thy head, and a cheyne of gold to thy necke.
My ſonne, <na>(g)</na> if ſinners shal entiſe thee, condeſcend not to them.

notes.label: g
notes.text: The ſecond to reſiſt euil ſuggeſtions.

verses.text: If they shal ſay: Come with vs, let vs lye in waite for bloud, let vs hide ſnares againſt the innocent without cauſe:
let vs swalow him aliue as hel, and whole as one deſcending into the lake.
We shal finde al precious ſubſtance, we shal fil our houſe with ſpoiles.
Caſt in thy lot with vs, let there be one purse of vs al.
My ſonne, walke not with them, ſtay thy foote from their pathes.
For their feete runne to euil, and make haſte to shede bloud.
But <na>(h)</na> a nette is caſt in vayne before the eies of them that haue winges.

notes.label: h
notes.text: The proper remedie againſt ſuch alurements is to be vvatchful, and to flee from them.

verses.text: Themſelues alſo lye in wayte againſt their owne bloud & practiſe deceites againſt their owne ſoules.
So the pathes of euerie couetous man, take violently the ſoules of the poſſeſſors.
Wiſdom preacheth abrode, she geueth her voice in the ſtreates:
In the head of multitudes she cryeth, in the doores of the gates of the citie she vttereth her wordes, ſaying:
O children how long doe you loue infancie, and fooles couet thoſe thinges, which are hurtful to them ſelues, and the vnwiſe hate knowlege?
Turne ye at my correction: behold I wil vtter my ſpirite to you, and wil shewe you my wordes.
Becauſe I called, and you refuſed: I ſtreched out my hand, and there was none that regarded.
You haue deſpiſed al my counſel, and haue neglected my reprehenſions.
I alſo wil laugh in your deſtruction, and wil ſcorne, when that shal come to you, which you feared.
When ſoden calamitie shal fal on you, and deſtruction, as a tempeſt shal be at hand: when tribulation, and diſtreſſe shal come vpon you:
Then shal they inuocate me, and I wil not heare: in the morning shal they ariſe, and shal not finde me:
for that they haue hated diſcipline, and not receiued the feare of our Lord,
nor conſented to my counſel, & detracted from al my correction.
They shal eate therefore the fruites of their way, and shal be filled with their owne counſels.
The auerſion of litle ones shal kil them, and the proſperitie of fooles shal deſtroy them.
But he that shal heare me, shal reſt without terrour, and shal enioy abundance, feare of euils being taken away.

chapters.summary: Parables are profitable to thoſe that loue and wil lerne wiſdom. 10. Al are admonished not to folow the alurements of ſinners: 20. but to embrace wiſdome; 24. and ruine is threatned to the contemners. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: The firſt part. And invitation to ſeek wiſdom: vvith ſome general precepts.

verses.text: MY ſonne, <na>(a)</na> if thou wilt receiue my wordes, and wilt hide my commandments with thee,

notes.label: a
notes.text: This frequent maner of propoſing the vvay and meanes to vviſdom If thou vvilt receiue my vvordes, &c. shevveth moſt euidently the povvre of mans free vvil.

verses.text: that thyne eare may heare wiſdom: incline thyne hart to knowe prudence.
For if thou shalt cal for wiſdom, and incline thyne hart to prudence:
If thou shalt ſeeke her <na>(b)</na> as money, and as treaſures shalt dig her vp:

notes.label: b
notes.text: Not euerie deſire, or ſleight ſeeking of vviſdom ſufficieth, but ſuch laborious ſeeking is required, as a couetous man ſeeketh treaſure vvhich he knoweth to be hid in the ground.

verses.text: then shalt thou vnderſtand the feare of our Lord, and shalt finde the knowlege of God.
Becauſe our Lord geueth wiſdom: and out of his mouth prudence and knowlege.
He wil keepe the ſaluation of the righteous, & protect them that walke ſimply
Keeping the pathes of iuſtice, & garding the wayes of ſaints.
Then shalt thou vnderſtand iuſtice, and iudgement, and equitie, and euery good path.
<cr>[1]</cr> If wiſdom shal enter into thy hart, and knowlege pleaſe thy ſoule:
counſel shal keepe thee, and prudence shal preſerue thee,
that thou mayſt be deliuered from the euil way, and from the man, that ſpeaketh peruerſe thinges:
<na>(c)</na> who leaue the right way, and walke by darke wayes:

notes.label: c
notes.text: A deſcription of peruers ſinners eſpecially of heretikes.

verses.text: who are glad when they haue done euil, and reioyce in moſt wicked thinges:
whoſe wayes are peruerſe, and their ſteppes infamous.
That thou mayſt be deliuered from the ſtrange woman, and from the forener, which mollifieth her wordes,
forſaketh the guide of her youth,
and hath forgotten the couenant of her God. For her houſe is bowed downe to death, and her pathes to hel.
Al that goe in vnto her, shal not returne neither shal they apprehend the pathes of life.
That thou mayſt walke in a good way: and mayſt keepe the pathes of the iuſt.
For they that are right, shal dwel in the earth, and the ſimple shal continue in it.
But the impious shal be deſtroyed from the earth: and they that doe vniuſtly shal be taken away from it.

chapters.summary: Gaining of wiſdom bringeth much good, 10. and auoydeth much euil: 16. deliuering from error of Idolaters and Hæretikes.

verses.text: MY ſonne, <na>(a)</na> forget not my law, and let thy <na>(b)</na> hart keepe my precepts.

notes.label: a
notes.text: It auaileth litle to heare good inſtructions, except vve kepe them in memorie.

notes.label: b
notes.text: not in books only but in the hart:

verses.text: For they shal adde to thee length of dayes, and yeares of life, and peace.
Let not <na>(c)</na> mercie and truth leaue thee, put them about thy throte; and write them in the tables of thy hart:
and thou shalt finde grace, and good diſcipline before God and men.
<na>(d)</na> Haue confidence in our Lord with al thy hart, and leane not vpon thyne owne prudence.

notes.label: d
notes.text: knovv alſo that al thy ſtreingth is in God, in vvhom thou maiſt ſecurely truſt, not in thyn ovvne prudence.

verses.text: In al thy wayes thinke on him, and he wil direct thy ſteppes.
Be not wiſe in thyne owne conceipte: feare God, and depart from euil:
for it shal be health to thy nauil, and watering of thy bones.
Honour our Lord with thy ſubſtance, and geue to him of the firſt of al thy fruites:
and thy barnes shal be replenished with fulnes, and thy preſſes shal runouer with wine.
My ſonne, caſt not away the diſcipline of our Lord: neither doe thou faint when thou art chaſteced of him:
<na>(e)</na> for whom our Lord loueth he chaſticeth: and as a father in the ſonne he pleaſeth himſelf.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Chaſtiſment and tribulation in thoſe that endeuour to ſerue God, is a ſigne of his fauour tovvards them; and therfore his other promiſes vvhich ſeme to be temporal, are to be vnderſtood of the next life.

verses.text: Bleſſed is the man that findeth wiſdom, and floweth with prudence:
better is the purchaſing therof then marchandiſe of ſiluer, and her fruite then chiefe and the pureſt gold:
she is more precious then al riches: and al thinges that are deſired, are not able to be compared with her.
<na>(f)</na> Length of dayes in her right hand, & in her left hand <na>(g)</na> riches and glorie

notes.label: f
notes.text: God revvardeth as it vvere vvith both handes promiſing eternal life,

notes.label: g
notes.text: and competent meanes in this life.

verses.text: Her wayes are beautiful wayes, and al her pathes peaceable.
She is a tree of life to them that shal apprehend her: and he that shal hold her is bleſſed.
Our Lord by wiſdom founded the earth, eſtablished the heauens by prudence.
By his wiſdom the depthes haue broken forth, and the cloudes waxe thicke with dew.
My ſonne, let not theſe thinges depart from thyne eies: kepe the law & counſel:
and there shal be life to thy ſoule, and <na>(h)</na> grace to thy iawes.

notes.label: h
notes.text: Merite for the wordes of thy mouth.

verses.text: Then shalt thou walke confidently in thy way, and thy foote shal not ſtumble:
if thou ſleepe, thou shalt not feare: thou shalt reſt, and thy ſleepe shal be ſweete.
Dread not at ſoden terrour, and the power of the impious falling vpon thee.
For our Lord wil be at thy ſide, and wil keepe thy foote that thou be not taken.
Doe not prohibite him to doe good, that is able: if thou be able, thy ſelfe alſo doe good.
Say not to thy frend: goe, and returne; and <na>(i)</na> to morow I wil geue to thee: wheras thou mayeſt geue forthwith.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Almes in ſeaſon is duble vvorth to that vvhich is differred long.

verses.text: Practiſe not euil againſt thy freind, when he hath affiance in thee.
Contend not againſt man without cauſe, wheras he hath done thee no euil.
Doe not enuie an vniuſt man, nor imitate his waies:
becauſe euerie deluder is an abomination of our Lord, and his communication is with the ſimple.
There is pouertie from our Lord in the houſe of the impious: but the habitations of the iuſt shal be bleſſed.
He shal delude the deluders, and to the milde he wil geue grace.
The wiſe shal poſſeſſe glorie: the exaltation of fooles ignominie.

chapters.summary: Wiſdom exhorteth to kepe Gods law ( geuing long life ) to obſerue mercie, and truth. 5. to confide in God, 7. to feare, 9. and honour him, 11. to take his correction gladly ( 13. for al good thinges folow wiſdom ) 27. to releue the needie without delay, 30. not to contend with the wicked, nor to imitate them. 33. The euil shal faile, and the godlie shal proſper.

verses.text: CHILDREN heare ye the fathers diſcipline, and attend that you may knowe prudence.
I wil geue you a good gift, forſake not my law.
For <na>(a)</na> I alſo was the ſonne of my father, tender and as onlie begotten in my mothers ſight:

notes.label: a
notes.text: As Salomon was inſtructed by his father king Dauid ſo he teacheth others, the right order novve to lerne vviſdom.

verses.text: and he taught me, & ſayd: Let thy hart receiue my wordes, kepe my preceptes, and thou shalt liue.
Poſſeſſe wiſedom, poſſeſſe prudence: forget not, neither decline from the wordes of my mouth.
Leaue her not, and she wil keepe thee: loue her, and she wil preſerue thee.
<na>(b)</na> The beginning of wiſdom, poſſeſſe wiſdom, and in al thy poſſeſſion purchaſe prudence:

notes.label: b
notes.text: The firſt part of wiſdom it is to deſire it. For nothing hindereth from being iuſt but that iuſtice is not deſired. S. Aug. in Pſal. 118. v. 20.

verses.text: take quickly, and she wil exalt thee: thou shalt be glorified of her, when thou shalt embrace her.
She wil geue to thy head increaſe of graces, and with a noble crowne she wil protect thee.
Heare my ſonne, and receiue my wordes, that yeares of life may be multiplied to thee.
The way of wiſdom I wil shew to thee, I wil leade thee by the pathes of equitie.
Which when thou shalt haue entered, thy ſteppes shal not be ſtraytened, and running thou shalt not haue a ſtumbling blocke.
Hold diſcipline, leaue it not: kepe it, becauſe the ſame is thy life.
Be not delighted in the pathes of the impious, neither let the way of the euil pleaſe thee.
Flee from it, neither paſſe thou by it: goe aſide, and forſake it.
For they ſleepe not vnleſſe they haue done il: and they take no ſleepe vnleſſe they ſupplant.
They eate the bread of impietie, and drinke the wine of iniquitie.
But the path of the iuſt, as shyning light proceedeth euen to perfect day.
The way of the impious is darkeſom: they know not where they fal.
My ſonne, heare my wordes, and incline thyne eare to my ſayinges.
Let them not depart from thyne eies, kepe them in the middes of thy hart.
For they are life to thoſe that finde them, and health to al flesh.
With al garde keepe thy <na>(c)</na> hart, becauſe life proceedeth from it.

notes.label: c
notes.text: As the hart is the principal part of the bodie, ſo the vvil is the chiefeſt povvre of the ſoule: from vvhich good or euil procedeth.

verses.text: Remoue from thee a froward mouth, and let detracting lippes be far from thee.
Let thyne eies ſee right thinges, & let thine eieliddes goe before thy ſteppes.
Direct the path to thy feete, and al thy wayes shal be eſtablished.
Decline not to the right hand, nor to the left: turne away thy foote from euil.
For our Lord knoweth the wayes that are on the right hand: but thoſe are peruers, which are on the left hand.
But he wil make thy courſes right, and thy wayes he wil bring forward in peace.

chapters.summary: The wiſeman exhorteth others by his owne example to ſeeke wiſdom, 14. to decline from the wicked, and to imitate the iuſt, 23. to guide wel the hart, mouth, and feete.

verses.text: MY ſonne, attend to my wiſdom, and to my prudence incline thyne eare,
that thou mayſt keepe <na>(a)</na> cogitations, and thy lippes preſerue diſcipline.

notes.label: a
notes.text: To auoide al impietie it is firſt of al neceſſarie, not to thinke, ſpeake, nor heare vnlawful thinges.

verses.text: Attend not to the deceipt of a <na>(b)</na> woman: for the lippes of an harlot are as a hony combe diſtilling, and her throte netter then oyle.

notes.label: b
notes.text: By woman is generally vnderſtood concupiſcence of vvhat ſinne ſoeuer, as ch. 1. v. 10. & ch 3. v. 33. chap. 4. v. 14.

verses.text: But her later endes are bitter as wormewood, and sharpe as a two edged ſword.
Her feete goe downe into death, and her steppes penetrate vnto hel.
They walke not by the path of life, her ſteppes are wandering, and vnſearcheable.
Now therfore my ſonne heare me, and depart not from the wordes of my mouth.
Make thy way far from her, and aproch not to the doores of her houſe.
Geue not thy honour <na>(c)</na> to ſtrangers, and thy yeres to the <na>(d)</na> cruel.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The vvorld the flesh and the diuel are ſtrangers.

notes.label: d
notes.text: And cruel enemies that render for revvard eternal damnation.

verses.text: Leſt perhaps ſtrangers be filled with thy ſtrength, and thy labours be in an other mans houſe,
and thou mourne in the end, when thou shalt haue ſpent thy flesh and thy bodie, and ſay:
Why haue I deteſted diſcipline, and my hart conſented not to reprehenſions,
nor I heard the voice of them that taught me, and haue not inclined mine eare to maſters?
I haue almoſt bene in al euil, in the middes of the church and of the ſynagoge.
Drinke water of thyne owne ceſterne, and the ſtremes of thy wel:
<na>(e)</na> Let thy fountaines be deriued abrode, and in the ſtreates diuide thy waters.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Good doctrine iſ to be imperted to men of ſincere intention.

verses.text: <na>(f)</na> Haue them alone, neither let ſtrangers be partakers with thee.

notes.label: f
notes.text: not to contemners and obſtinate infidels.

verses.text: Let thy vayne be bleſſed, and reioyce with the woman of thy youth:
a hinde moſt deare, and a moſt grateful fawne: let her breaſtes inebriate thee at al time, in her loue be thou delighted continually.
Why art thou ſeduced my ſonne of a ſtrange woman, and art cherished in the boſome of an other?
Our Lord beholdeth the wayes of a man, and conſidereth al his ſteppes.
His owne iniquities take the impious, and he is faſt bonde with the ropes of his ſinnes.
He shal die becauſe he hath not had diſcipline, and in the multitude of his folie he shal be deceiued.

chapters.summary: Againe wiſdom dehorteth from fornication ( carnal and ſpiritual ) 6. shewing that in the end ſinners shal ſee and feele the effect of their follie: 20. which God ſeeth and wil punish.

verses.text: MY ſonne, <na>(a)</na> if thou shalt be ſuretie for thy freind, and haſt made faſt thy hand to a ſtranger,

notes.label: a
notes.text: The wiſman doth not abſolutly diſſwade from al maner of ſuretishippe, but from rashly, or vnaduiſedly anſwering for others. And eſpecially exhorteth to vſe al diligence in performing, or cauſing others to performe that vvhich is promiſed or couenanted.

verses.text: thou art entrapped with the wordes of thy mouth, & caught with thyne owne wordes.
Doe therefore my ſonne that which I ſay, and deliuer thyſelfe, becauſe thou art fallen into the hand of thy neighbour. Runne diuers wayes, make haſt, rayſe thy freind:
Geue not ſleepe to thine eies, neither let thine eieliddes ſlumber.
Deliuer thyſelfe as a litle doa from the hand, and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.
Goe to the emmote ô ſluggard, and conſider her wayes, and lerne wiſdom.
Who wheras she hath no guide, nor maſter, nor captaine,
prepareth meate for herſelfe in the ſummer, and gethereth in the harueſt for to eate
How long wilt thou ſleepe ô ſluggard? when wilt thou riſe out of thy ſleepe?
Thou shalt sleepe a litle, a litle shalt thou ſlumber, a litle shalt thou ioyne thy handes to ſleepe:
and penurie shal come to thee, as a wayfaring man, and pouertie as a man armed. But if thou be not ſluggish, thy harueſt shal come as a fountaine, and penurie shal flee farre from thee.
A man that is an <na>(b)</na> Apoſtata, a man vnprofitable, goeth with peruerſe mouth,

notes.label: b
notes.text: Euerie one that ſinneth vvittingly and of malice refuſing to obey God, imployeth his mouth, eies, feete, handes and al partes with a wicked hart and intention to peruerte others: moſt proper to heretikes, apoſtates from the faith.

verses.text: winketh with the eies, treadeth with the foote, ſpeaketh with the finger,
with wicked hart he deuiſeth euil, and at al time he ſoweth brawles.
To him his deſtruction shal come forthwith, and he shal ſodenlie be deſtroyed, neither shal he haue remedie any more.
Six thinges there are, which our Lord hateth, and the ſeuenth his ſoule deteſteth:
Loftie eies, a lying tongue, handes that shede innocent bloud,
a hart that deuiſeth moſt wicked deuiſes, feete ſwift to runne into euil,
a deceitful witneſſe that vttereth lies, and him that among brether <na>(c)</na> ſoweth diſcordes.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The former ſix are al damnable, but this ſeuenth is moſt deteſtable, becauſe it is oppoſite to the chief vertue charitie, it breaketh vnitie, & is the proper ſinne of the diuel.

verses.text: My ſonne keepe the preceptes of thy father, and leaue not the lawe of thy mother.
Bynde them in thy hart continualy, and put them about thy throte.
When thou shalt walke, let them goe with thee: when thou shalt ſleepe, let them kepe thee, and awaking talke with them.
Becauſe the commandment is a lampe, and the lawe a light, and the way of life the increpation of diſcipline:
that they may kepe thee from the euil woman, and from the faire ſpoken tongue of the ſtranger.
Let not thy hart couet her beautie, be not caught with her beckes:
for the price of an harlot is ſcarſe worth one loafe: but a woman catcheth the precious ſoule of man.
<na>(d)</na> Can a man hide fyre in his boſome, that his garmentes burne not?

notes.label: d
notes.text: Al occaſions of ſinne, eſpecially probable are to be shunned.

verses.text: Or walke vpon hote coales, that his ſoales be not burnt?
ſo he that goeth in vnto his neighbours wife, shal not be cleane when he shal touche her.
It is <na>(e)</na> no greate fault, when a man shal haue ſtollen: for he ſtealeth to fil his hungrie ſoule:

notes.label: e
notes.text: Theft is alſo mortal ſinne, againſt the ſeuenth cōmandment, but not ſo great as adulterie.

verses.text: alſo being taken he shal reſtore ſeuenfold, and shal geue vp al the ſubſtance of his houſe.
But he that is an aduouterer, for penurie of hart shal deſtroy his owne ſoule:
shame and ignominie he gethereth to himſelfe, & his reproch shal not be blotted out.
Becauſe the zele and furie of the husband wil not ſpare in the day of reuenge,
neither wil he yeld to any mans prayers, neither wil he take for redemption verie many giftes.

chapters.summary: He that is ſuretie for an other, muſt haue care to diſcharge that he promiſeth. 6. The ſlouthful muſt lerne diligence of the emmotte. 12. The deſcription of an Apoſtata. 16. Aboue other ſix bad thinges, God deteſteth the ſower of diſcord. 20. Al are exhorted to kepe Gods law, 24. namely to flee fornication, and al occaſions therof.

verses.text: MY ſonne, <na>(a)</na> keepe my wordes, and my preceptes hide with thee. Sonne,

notes.label: a
notes.text: Becauſe tentations ſtil occurre in this life, and man is fraile, good exhortations, and earneſt admonitions muſt alſo be continualy inculcated, as here the vviſman often repeteth and much vrgeth the ſame good and neceſſarie aduiſes to embrace vviſdom and to vvalke ſtil in the way of vertue, eſpecially to flee from vices, and dangers of ſinne.

verses.text: keepe my commandmentes, and thou shalt liue: and my law as the apple of thine eie:
binde it on thy fingers, write it in the tables of thy hart.
Say to wiſdom, thou art my ſiſter: & cal prudence thy freind,
that she may keepe thee from the ſtrange woman, and from the forener which maketh her wordes ſweete.
For out of the window of my houſe I looked out through the lattiſe,
and I ſee litle ones, I behold a foolish youngman,
which paſſeth through the ſtreates by the corner, and goeth nigh the way of her houſe,
in the darke the day being toward euening, in the darkenes of the night, and dimnes,
And behold the woman meeteth him in harlotes atyre, prepared to deceiue ſoules: babling and wandering,
impatient of reſt, nor able to conſiſt in the houſe on her feete,
now abrode, now in the ſtreates, now lying in wayte neere the corners.
And taking the youngman she kiſſeth him, and with malepert countenance ſpeaketh fayre, ſaying:
I vowed victimes for welfare, this day I haue payed my vowes.
Therfore I am come forth to meete thee, deſirous to ſee thee, and I haue found thee.
I haue wouen my bed with cordes, I haue adorned it with tapeſtrie pictured out of Ægypt.
I haue ſprinkled my bed with myrrhe, aloes, and cinamome.
Come let vs be inebriated with breſtes, and let vs enioy deſired embracings, til the day appeare.
For my huſband is not at home, he is gone a very long iourney.
he caried with him a bagge of money: in the day of the ful moone he wil returne to his houſe.
She intangled him with many wordes, and with flatterie of lippes drewe him.
Immediatly he foloweth her <na>(b)</na> as an oxe led to be a victime, & as a lambe playing the wanton, and not knowing that he is drawen as a foole to bondes,

notes.label: b
notes.text: Sinners after conſent geuen to tentations, are as inconſiderate of their ovvne ſtate, & of their perile and ruine, as an oxe, vvhen he iſ ledde to the shamles, or a bird allured vvith a bate, that flieth into the ſnare or nette.

verses.text: til the arow pearſe his liuer: as if a birde should make haſte to the ſnare, and knoweth not that his life is in danger.
Now therfore my ſonne, heare me, and attend to the wordes of my mouth.
Let not thy mind be drawen away in her wayes: neither be thou deceiued with her pathes.
For she hath caſt downe manie wounded, and al the moſt ſtrong are ſlaine by her.
Her houſe the wayes of hel, penetrating to the inner partes of death.

chapters.summary: He further exhorteth yongmen to ſeke wiſdom, 5. eſpecially to flee from the intiſements of harlots, largely deſcribing the ſame, 22. and the ruine of them that are ſo deluded.

verses.text: DOTH not wiſdom crie, and prudence geue her voice?
Standing <na>(a)</na> in the high & loftie toppes ouer the way, in the middes of the pathes,

notes.label: a
notes.text: True wiſdom directing to good life, & ſo to eternal ſaluation, is only found in the viſible Church ſtanding vpon a mountaine, not hidde in corners or obſcure places.

verses.text: beſide the gates of the citie, in the verie doores she ſpeaketh, ſaying:
O men, to you I crie, and my voice is to the children of men.
O litle ones vnderſtand ſubtiltie, and ye vnwiſe marke.
Heare ye, becauſe I wil ſpeake of great thinges: and my lippes shal be opened to preach right thinges.
My throte shal meditate truth, and my lippes shal deteſt the impious.
Al my wordes are iuſt, there is no wicked, nor peruerſe thing in them.
They are right to them that vnderſtand, and iuſt to them that finde knowlege.
Receiue ye diſcipline, & not money: chooſe doctrine rather then gold.
For wiſdom is better then al moſt precious riches: and whatſoeuer is to be deſired can not be compared to it.
I <na>(b)</na> wiſdome dwel in counſel, and am preſent in lerned cogitations.

notes.label: b
notes.text: Theſe ſingular praiſes perteine to the increated wiſdom, God himſelf, from whom procedeth wiſdom geuen to men by the Holie Ghoſt. See Annot. ch. 1. v. 2.

verses.text: The feare of our Lord hateth euil: arrogancie, and pride, and wicked way, and a duble roungued mouth I doe deteſt.
Myne is counſel & equitie, prudence is mine, ſtrength is mine.
By me kinges doe reigne, and the makers of law decree iuſt thinges.
By me princes rule, and the mightie decree iuſtice.
I loue them that loue me: and they that watch toward me shal finde me.
With me are riches, and glorie, glorious riches, and iuſtice.
For my fruite is better then gold, and precious ſtone, and my bloſomes then choſen ſiluer.
I walke in the wayes of iuſtice, in the middes of the pathes of iudgement,
that I may enriche them that loue me, and may replenish their treaſures.
Our Lord poſſeſſed me in the beginning of his wayes, before he had made any thing from the beginning.
From eternitie I was ordayned & of old before the earth was made.
The depthes were not as yet, and I was now conceiued, neither had the fountaines of waters as yet gushed forth:
the mountaines with heauie hugeneſſe ſtoode not as yet: before the litle hilles I was brought forth:
he had not yet made the earth, and the riuers, and the poles of the round world.
When he prepared the heauens, I was preſent: when with a certaine law, and circuite he compaſſed the depthes:
When he eſtablished the firmament aboue, & poyſed the fountaines of waters:
when he compaſſed the ſea with her limites, and ſet a law to the waters that they should not paſſe their boundes: when he hanged the foundations of the earth.
I was with him, framing al thinges: and was delighted euerie day, playing before him at al time;
playing in the world: & <na>(c)</na> my delights to be with the children of men.

notes.label: c
notes.text: God much preferreth man before al other corporal creatures.

verses.text: Now therfore children heare me: bleſſed are they, that keepe my wayes.
Heare ye diſcipline, and be wiſe, and reiect it not.
Bleſſed is the man that heareth me, & that watcheth at my doores dayly, & wayteth at the poſtes of my doore.
He that shal finde me, shal finde life, and shal draw ſaluation of our Lord:
but he that shal ſinne againſt me, shal hurt his owne ſoule. Al that hate me, loue death.

chapters.summary: Wiſdom is preached in conſpicuous and moſt frequented places, that none may pretend wante of admonition, 7. her doctrin is true, godlie, profitable, & neceſſarie to al ſortes of men. 12. wiſdom (increated which is God himſelfe) is eternal. 32. and bringeth eternal happines.

verses.text: WISEDOME hath built herſelf an houſe, she hath cut out ſeuen pillers.
She hath immolated her victimes, mingled her wine, and ſet forth her table.
She hath ſent her handmaides to cal to the towre, and to the walles of the citie:
If any be a litle one, let him come to me. And to the vnwiſe she ſpake:
Come, <na>(a)</na> eate ye my bread, & drinke the wine which I haue mingled for you.

notes.label: a
notes.text: S. Cyprian li. 1. ep. 3. citeth this whole paſſage of Chriſts Sacrifice in the formes of bread and wine.

verses.text: Leaue infancie, and liue, and walke by the wayes of prudence.
He that teacheth a ſcorner doth iniurie to himſelf; and he that rebuketh the impious, purchaſeth a blotte to himſelf.
Rebuke <na>(b)</na> not the ſcorner leſt hee hate thee. <na>(c)</na> Rebuke a wiſe man, and he wil loue thee.

notes.label: b
notes.text: VVhere is no hope of amendment prudence directeth vs not to admonish, nor rebuke ſinners, leſt without anie fruite we procure emnitie. charitie alſo requireth rather to expect better opportunitie, leſt the offender become worſe by our admonition.

notes.label: c
notes.text: But when there is hope of good, euerie one is bond, eſpecially ſuperiors to correct offenders. S. Aug. li. 1. c. 9. de ciuit. S. Baſil. regulis fuſe diſput. 158.

verses.text: Geue occaſion to a wiſe man, and wiſdom shal be added to him. Teach the iuſt, and he shal make haſte to take it.
The beginning of wiſdom, the feare of our Lord: and the knowlege of the holie, prudence.
For by me shal thy dayes be multiplied, and yeres of life shal be added to thee.
If thou be wiſe, to thyſelf thou shalt be: and if a ſcorner, thou alone shalt beare the euil.
A foolish woman and clamorous, and ful of alurementes, and knowing nothing at al,
ſate in the doores of her houſe vpon a ſeate in a high place of the citie,
to cal them that paſſe by the way, and goe on their iourney:
He that is a litle one, let him turne to me. And to the foole she ſpake:
Stolen waters are ſweeter, and hidden bread more pleaſant.
and he was ignorant that giantes are there, and her gueſtes in the depthes of hel.

chapters.summary: Wiſdom hauing built her houſe with ſeuen pillers, inuiteth al to a prepared banquette, 11. promiſing to multiplie ioyful dayes. 13. Folie inciteth to her contrarie banquet of ſtollen water and hidde bread.

summary_continuation.text: banquet of ſtollen water and hidde bread.

verses.text: A wiſe ſonne maketh the father glad: but a foolish ſonne is the ſorow of his mother. <na>[1]</na>
The treaſures of impietie shal profit nothing: but iuſtice shal deliuer from death. <na>[1]</na>
Our Lord wil not afflict with famine the ſoule of the iuſt, and the deceitful practiſes of the impious he wil ouerthrow. <na>[1]</na>

The ſlothful hand hath wrought pouertie: the hand of the ſtrong getteth riches. <na>[1]</na> Who ſo truſteth to lyes feedeth the windes: and the ſelfe ſame man foloweth the flying birdes. <na>[2]</na>
He that gathereth in the harueſt, is a wiſe ſonne: but he that ſnorteth in ſummer, is the ſonne of confuſion. <na>[1]</na>
The bleſſing of our Lord is vpon the head of the iuſt: but iniquitie couereth the mouth of the impious. <na>[1]</na>
The memorie of the iuſt is with prayſes: and the name of the impious shal rotte. <na>[1]</na>
The wiſe of hart shal receiue preceptes: a foole is beaten with lippes. <na>[1]</na>
He that walketh playnly, walketh confidently: but he that depraueth his wayes, shal be manifeſt. <na>[1]</na>
He that wincketh with the eye, shal geue ſorow: and the foole in lippes shal be beaten. <na>[1]</na>
A vayne of life, the mouth of the iuſt: and the mouth of the impious couereth iniquitie. <na>[1]</na>
Hatred rayſeth brawles: and charitie couereth al ſinnes. <na>[1]</na>
In the lippes of the wiſe wiſdom is found: and a rod on his backe that lacketh witte. <na>[1]</na>
Wiſe men hide knowlege: but the mouth of the foole is next to confuſion. <na>[1]</na>
The ſubſtance of a rich man, is a citie of his ſtrength: the feare of the poore their pouertie. <na>[1]</na>
The worke of the iuſt vnto life: but the fruite of the impious vnto ſinne. <na>[1]</na>
The way of life, to him that keepeth diſcipline: but he that forſaketh reprehenſions, erreth. <na>[1]</na>
Lying lippes hide hatred; he that vttereth contumelie is vnwiſe. <na>[1]</na>
In much talke there shal not want ſinne: but he that moderateth his lippes is moſt wiſe. <na>[1]</na>
The tongue of the iuſt, is choſen ſiluer: but the hart of the impious is nothing worth. <na>[1]</na>
The lippes of the iuſt teach verie many: but they that are vntaught, shal die in the penurie of witte. <na>[1]</na>
The bleſſing of our Lord maketh men rich: neither shal affliction be ioyned to them. <na>[1]</na>
A foole worketh miſcheefe as it were by laughter: but wiſdom is prudence to a man. <na>[1]</na>
That which the impious feareth, shal come vpon him: to the iuſt their deſire shal be geuen. <na>[1]</na>
As a tempeſt paſſing the impious shal not be: but the iuſt as an euerlaſting fundation. <na>[1]</na>
As vinegre to the teeth, and ſmoke to the eies, ſo a ſluggard to them, that ſent him. <na>[1]</na>
The feare of our Lord shal adde dayes: and the yeares of the impious shal be shortened. <na>[1]</na>
The expectation of the iuſt is ioy: but the hope of the impious shal perish. <na>[1]</na>
The ſtrength of the ſimple the way of our Lord: and feare is to them that worke euil. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Obſeruation of Gods law, fulfulling al iuſtice.

verses.text: The iuſt for euer shal not be moued: but the impious shal not dwel on the earth.
The mouth of the iuſt shal bring forth wiſdom: the tongue of the froward shal perish. <na>[1]</na>
The lippes of the iuſt conſider gratful thinges: and the mouth of the impious peruerſe thinges.

articles.title: THE PARABLES OF SALOMON.
articles.text: This repetition of the title signifieth, that the sentences which follow are more properly called <mn>[1]</mn> Parables, than the former: From which they also differ in manner of utterance, by the figure Antithesis, for most part opposing, and comparing contrary virtues and vices, shewing their contrary effects; with great elegancy, especially in the original tongue; which could not be so fully expressed in Greek, nor Latin, much less in vulgar language: But are the same in sense, though <mn>[2]</mn> often obscure, by reason of the Hebrew phrase, shortness of sentences, and so without any certain connexion, that we cannot with perspicuity, comprehend the sum thereof in brief contents, after the ordinary manner before the chapters. And therefore have thought it better for the vulgar reader, to set down in the margent of the twenty chapters next following, in brief terms, the <mn>[3]</mn> virtues, or other good things (rather than the bad, not having place for both) commended in every sentence. For though the same be not always expressed in the text, yet they may be understood by their opposite vices. Whosoever desireth further explication, may find many of these divine sentences excellently expounded by S. Jerome. S. Augustine, S. Gregory and other Fathers in several places. Or read S. Beda's Commentaries upon this whole book, To. 4. Vel apud S. Jerome. To. 7. Or amongst late writers, our learned countryman D. Radulphus Bainus, Bishop Jansenius, and F. Peltanus.

notes.text: The second part. Sententious moral precepts.
How these Parables following differ from the former.
Why the contents of the twenty chapters following are put in the margent.

verses.text: A deceitful balance, is abomination before God: and an equal weight is his wil. <na>[1]</na>
Where pride shal be, there shal be contumelie alſo: but where humilitie, there alſo wiſdom. <na>[1]</na>
The ſimplicitie of the iuſt shal direct them: and the ſupplanting of the peruers shal waſte them. <na>[1]</na>
Riches shal not profit in the day of reuenge: but iuſtice shal deliuer from death. <na>[1]</na>
The iuſtice of the ſimple shal direct his way: and the impious shal fal in his impietie. <na>[1]</na>
The iuſtice of the righteous shal deliuer them: and the vniuſt shal be caught in their deceitful practiſes. <na>[1]</na>
The impious man being dead, there shal be no hope any more: and the expectation of the careful shal perish. <na>[1]</na>
The iuſt is deliuered from diſtreſſe: and the impious shal be geuen for him. <na>[1]</na>
The diſſembler with his mouth deceiueth his freind: but the iuſt shal be deliuered by knowlege. <na>[1]</na>
In the good thinges of the iuſt the citie shal reioyce; and in the deſtruction of the impious there shal be prayſe. <na>[1]</na>
With the benediction of the iuſt the citie shal be exalted: and by the mouth of the impious it shal be ſubuerted. <na>[1]</na>
He that deſpiſeth his freind, lacketh hart: but the wiſe man wil hold his peace. <na>[1]</na>
He that walketh fraudulently, reueleth ſecretes: but he that is faithful, concealeth the thing comitted of his freind. <na>[1]</na>
Where there is no gouernour, the people shal fal: but there is health where is much counſel. <na>[1]</na>
He shal be afflicted with euil, that is ſuretie for a ſtranger: but he that is ware of the ſnares, shal be ſecure. <na>[1]</na>
A gracious woman shal finde glorie: and the ſtrong shal haue riches. <na>[1]</na>
A merciful man doth good to his kinred alſo. <na>[1]</na>
The impious maketh an vnſtable worke: but to him that ſoweth iuſtice, is a faythful reward. <na>[1]</na>
Clemencie prepareth life: & the purſewing of euil thinges death. <na>[1]</na>
A peruers hart is abominable to our Lord: and his wil is in them that walke ſimply. <na>[1]</na>
Hand in hand the euil man shal not be innocent: but the ſeede of the iuſt shal be ſaued. <na>[1]</na>
A ring of gold in a ſwines ſnoute, a fayre woman & a foole. <na>[1]</na>
The deſire of the iuſt is al good: the expectation of the impious furie. <na>[1]</na>
Some diuide their owne goodes, and are made richer: others take violently not their owne, and are alwayes in pouertie. <na>[1]</na>
The ſoule which bleſſeth, shal be made fatte: and he that inebriateth himſelf shal alſo be inebriated. <na>[1]</na>
He that hydeth corne, shal be curſed among the peoples: but bleſſing vpon the head of them that ſel. <na>[1]</na>
Wel riſeth he early who ſeeketh good thinges: but he that is a ſearcher after euil thinges, shal be oppreſſed of them. <na>[1]</na>
He that truſteth in his riches shal fal: but the iuſt shal ſpring as a greene leafe. <na>[1]</na>
He that troubleth his houſe, shal poſſeſſe the windes: and he that is a foole shal ſerue the wiſe. <na>[1]</na>
The fruite of the iuſt man a tree of life: and he that gaineth ſoules, is wiſe. <na>[1]</na>
If the iuſt man receiue in the earth, how much more the impious and ſinner? <na>[1]</na>
HE that loueth diſcipline, loueth knowlege: but he that hateth reprehenſions is vnwiſe. <na>[1]</na>
He that is good, shal draw grace from our Lord: but he that truſteth in his owne cogitation, doth impiouſly. <na>[1]</na>
Man shal not be ſtrengthened by impietie: and the roote of the iuſt shal not be moued. <na>[1]</na>
A diligent woman is a crowne to her husband: and putrefaction in his bones, she that doth thinges worthie of confuſion. <na>[1]</na>
The cogitations of the iuſt are iudgements: & the counſels of the impious are fraudulent. <na>[1]</na>
The wordes of the impious lie in wayte for bloud: the mouth of the iuſt shal deliuer them. <na>[1]</na>
Turne the impious, and they shal not be: but the houſe of the iuſt shal be permanent. <na>[1]</na>
A man shal be knowen by his doctrine: but he that is vaine and foolish, shal lye open to contempt. <na>[1]</na>
Better is the poore and ſufficient to himſelf, then he that is glorious and wanteth bread. <na>[1]</na>
The iuſt knoweth the liues of his beaſtes: but the bowels of the impious are cruel. <na>[1]</na>

He that tilleth his land, shal be filled with breads: but he that purſeweth idlenes is a verie foole. <na>[1]</na> He that is delighted in much quaffing of wine, leaueth contumelie in his munitions. <na>[2]</na>
The deſire of the impious is the <na>[1]</na> muniment of the moſt wicked: but the roote of the iuſt shal proſper. <na>[2]</na>

notes.text: defence · Iuſt punishment of the wicked.

verses.text: For the ſinnes of the lippes ruine approcheth to the euil man: but the iuſt eſcapeth out of diſtreſſe. <na>[1]</na>
Of the fruite of his owne mouth shal euerie man be replenished with good thinges, and according to the workes of his handes it shal be repayed him. <na>[1]</na>
The way of a foole is right in his eies: but he that is wiſe heareth counſels. <na>[1]</na>
A foole by & by sheweth his anger: but he that diſſembleth iniuries is wiſe. <na>[1]</na>
He that ſpeaketh that which he knoweth, is an vtterer of iuſtice: but he that lyeth, is a fraudulent witneſſe. <na>[1]</na>
There is that promiſeth, and is pricked as it were with the ſword of conſcience: but the tongue of the wiſe is health. <na>[1]</na>
The lippe of truth shal be ſtable for euer: but he that is an haſtie witneſſe, frameth a tongue of lying. <na>[1]</na>
Guile is in the hart of them that thinke euil thinges: but ioy foloweth them that geue counſels of peace. <na>[1]</na>
It shal not make the iuſt ſorie what ſoeuer shal fal to him: but the impious shal be replenished with euil. <na>[1]</na>
Lying lippes are an abomination to our Lord: but they that doe faithfully pleaſe him. <na>[1]</na>
A circumſpect man concealeth knowlege: and the hart of the vnwiſe prouoketh folie. <na>[1]</na>
The hand of the ſtrong shal rule, but that which is ſlothful, shal ſerue vnder tributes. <na>[1]</na>
Penſifneſſe in the hart of a man shal humble him, & with a good word he shal be made glad. <na>[1]</na>
He that neglecteth damage for a freind, is iuſt: but the way of the impious shal deceiue them. <na>[1]</na>
The fraudulent man shal not finde gayne: and the ſubſtance of a <na>[1]</na> man shal be the price of gold. <na>[2]</na>
In the path of iuſtice, life: but the byway leadeth to death. <na>[1]</na>
A wiſe ſonne, is the doctrine of the father: but he that is a ſcorner, heareth not when he is rebuked. <na>[1]</na>
Of the fruite of his owne mouth man shal be filled with good thinges: but the ſoule of the preuaricatours is wicked. <na>[1]</na>
He that kepeth his mouth, kepeth his ſoule: but he that is vnaduiſed to ſpeake shal feele euils. <na>[1]</na>
The ſluggard wil and wil not: but the ſoule of them that worke, shal be made fatte. <na>[1]</na>
The iuſt shal deteſt a lying word: but the impious confoundeth, and shal be confounded. <na>[1]</na>
Iuſtice kepeth the way of the innocent: but impietie ſupplanteth the ſinner. <na>[1]</na>
There is one as it were with riches wheras he hath nothing: and there is as it were poore, wheras he is in much riches. <na>[1]</na>
The redemption of a mans life, his riches: but he that is poore, beareth not reprehenſion. <na>[1]</na>
The light of the iuſt maketh glad: but the candle of the impious shal be extinguished. <na>[1]</na>
Among the prowde there are alwayes brawles: but they that doe al thinges with counſel, are ruled by wiſdom. <na>[1]</na>
Subſtance haſtened shal be diminished: but that which by litle and litle is gathered with the hand, shal be multiplied. <na>[1]</na>
Hope that is differred afflicteth the ſoule: a tree of life the deſire of coming. <na>[1]</na>

Who ſo detracteth from any thing, he byndeth himſelfe for the time to come: but he that feareth the precept, shal conuers in peace. <na>[1]</na> Guilful ſoules erre in ſinnes: the iuſt are merciful & haue pitie. <na>[2]</na>
The law of a wiſe man a fountaine of life, that he may decline from the ruine of death. <na>[1]</na>
Good doctrine shal geue grace: in the way of contemners a whirlepoole. <na>[1]</na>
The ſubtel man doth al thinges with counſel: but he that is a foole openeth folie. <na>[1]</na>
The meſſenger of the impious shal fal into euil: but a faithful legate, is health. <na>[1]</na>
Pouertie, and ignominie, to him that forſaketh diſcipline: but he that yeldeth to him that rebuketh, shal be glorified. <na>[1]</na>
Deſire if it be accomplished, delighteth the ſoule: fooles deteſt them that flee euil thinges. <na>[1]</na>
He that walketh with the wiſe, shal be wiſe: a freind of fooles shal be made like. <na>[1]</na>
Euil purſeweth ſinners, and to the iuſt good thinges shal be repayed. <na>[1]</na>
The good man leaueth heyres, ſonnes and nephewes: and the ſubſtance of the ſinner is kept for the iuſt. <na>[1]</na>
Much meate in the tilled growndes of the fathers: and to others they are gathered without iudgement. <na>[1]</na>
He that ſpareth the rod, hateth his childe: but he that loueth him doth inſtantly nurture him. <na>[1]</na>
The iuſt eateth and filleth his ſoule: but the bellie of the impious vnſatiable. <na>[1]</na>
A wiſe woman buildeth her houſe: the vnwiſe wil with her handes deſtroy that alſo which is built. <na>[1]</na>
He that walketh in the right way, & feareth God is deſpiſed of him, that goeth an infamous way. <na>[1]</na>
In the mouth of a foole the rod of pride: but the lippes of the wiſe keepe them. <na>[1]</na>
Where oxen are not, the ſtal is emptie: but where much corne is, there is the oxes ſtrength manifeſt. <na>[1]</na>
A faithful witneſſe wil not lie: but a deceitful witneſſe vttereth a lie. <na>[1]</na>
A ſcorner ſeeketh wiſdom and findeth it not: the doctrine of the prudent is eaſie. <na>[1]</na>
Goe againſt a foolish man, and he knoweth not the lippes of prudence. <na>[1]</na>
The wiſdom of a diſcrete man is to vnderſtand his way: and the imprudence of fooles erreth. <na>[1]</na>
A foole wil laugh at ſinne, & among the iuſt grace shal abide. <na>[1]</na>
The hart that knoweth the bitternes of his ſoule, in his ioy shal not the ſtranger be mingled. <na>[1]</na>
The houſe of the impious shal be raſed: the tabernacles of the iuſt shal ſpring. <na>[1]</na>
There is a way, which ſeemeth to a man iuſt: but the later endes therof lead to death. <na>[1]</na>
Laughter shal be mingled with ſorow, and mourning occupieth the later endes of ioy. <na>[1]</na>
A foole shal be replenished with his wayes, and the good man shal be aboue him. <na>[1]</na>
The innocent beleueth euerie word: the diſcrete man conſidereth his ſteppes. <na>[1]</na>
A wiſe man feareth and declineth from euil: the foole leapeth ouer and is confident. <na>[1]</na>
The impatient man shal worke folie: and the ſubtel man is odious. <na>[1]</na>
<cr>[1]</cr> The childish man shal poſſeſſe folie, and the prudent shal expect knowlege. <na>[2]</na>
The euil shal lie downe before the good, and the impious before the gates of the iuſt. <na>[1]</na>
The poore shal be odious euen to his neighbour: but the freindes of the rich be manie. <na>[1]</na>
He that deſpiſeth his neighbour, ſinneth: but he that hath pitie on the poore, shal be bleſſed. <na>[1]</na>
They erre that worke euil: mercie and truth prepare good thinges. <na>[1]</na>
In euerie worke there shal be abundance: but where manie wordes are, there is oftentimes pouertie. <na>[1]</na>
The crowne of the wiſe, their riches: the follie of fooles, inprudence. <na>[1]</na>
A faithful witnes deliuereth ſoules: and the <na>[1]</na> diſſembler vttereth lyes. <na>[2]</na>
In the feare of our Lord is confidence of ſtrength, and to his children there shal be hope. <na>[1]</na>
The feare of our Lord a fountaine of life, that he may decline from the ruine of death. <na>[1]</na>
In the multitude of people the dignitie of the king: and in fewnes of people the ignominie of the prince. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Procure loue and fidelitie in ſubiectes.

verses.text: He that is patient, is gouerned with much wiſdom: but he that is impatient, exalteth his follie. <na>[1]</na>
Health of hart, the life of the flesh: enuie, the putrefaction of the bones. <na>[1]</na>
He that doth calumniate the needie, vpbraideth his maker: but he honoreth him, that hath pitie on the poore. <na>[1]</na>
The impious shal be expelled in his malice: but the iuſt hopeth in his death. <na>[1]</na>
In the hart of the prudent reſteth wiſdom, & it shal inſtruct al the vnlerned. <na>[1]</na>
Iuſtice aduanceth a nation: but ſinne maketh peoples miſerable. <na>[1]</na>
A ſeruant that vnderſtandeth is acceptable to the king: he that is vnprofitable shal ſuſteyne his anger. <na>[1]</na>
A ſoft anſwer breaketh anger: and a hard word rayſeth vp furie. <na>[1]</na>
The tongue of the wiſe adorneth knowlege: the mouth of fooles boyleth forth follie. <na>[1]</na>
In euerie place the eies of our Lord behold the good and the euil. <na>[1]</na>
A peaceable tongue is a tree of life: but that which is immoderate, shal breake the ſpirite. <na>[1]</na>

A foole ſcorneth the diſcipline of his father: but he that regardeth reprehenſions, shal become more prudent. <na>[1]</na> In abundant iuſtice there is greateſt force: but the cogitations of the impious shal be rooted out.
The houſe of the iuſt is very much ſtrength: and in the fruites of the impious is perturbation. <na>[1]</na>
The lippes of the wiſe shal ſow knowlege: the hart of fooles shal be vnlike. <na>[1]</na>
The victimes of the impious are abominable to our Lord: the vowes of the iuſt are acceptable. <na>[1]</na>
The way of the impious is abomination to our Lord: he that foloweth iuſtice is beloued of him. <na>[1]</na>
The doctrine is euil of them that forſake the way of life: he that hateth reprehenſions shal dye.
Hel, and perdition are before our Lord: how much more the hartes of the children of men? <na>[1]</na>
The peſtilent man loueth not him, that rebuketh him: nor goeth to the wiſe. <na>[1]</na>
A glad hart cheereth the face: in pensifnes of minde the ſpirit is caſt downe. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: A cherful hart is deſirous to lerne.

verses.text: The hart of the wiſe ſeeketh doctrine: and the mouth of fooles is fed with vnskilfulnes.
Al the dayes of the poore are euil: a ſecure minde is as it were a continual feaſt. <na>[1]</na>
Better is a litle with the feare of our Lord, then great treaſures and vnſatiable. <na>[1]</na>
It is better to be called to herbes with charitie: then to a fatted calfe with hatred.
An angrie man ſtirreth brawles: he that is patient appeaſeth thoſe that are raiſed. <na>[1]</na>
The way of the ſlothful is as an hedge of thornes: the way of the iuſt is without offence. <na>[1]</na>
A wiſe ſonne maketh the father ioyful: and the foolish man deſpiſeth his mother. <na>[1]</na>
Follie is ioy to a foole: and the wiſeman directeth his ſteppes. <na>[1]</na>
Cogitations are diſſipated where there is no counſel: but where manie counſellers are, they are confirmed. <na>[1]</na>
A man reioyceth in the ſentence of his mouth: and a word in due time is beſt. <na>[1]</na>
The path of life aboue the lerned, that he may decline from the laweſt hel. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: To him that is wel trained in good workes, heauen gates are open.

verses.text: Our Lord wil deſtroy the houſe of the proude: and wil make ſure the borders of the widow.
Euil cogitations are an abomination to our Lord: and pure ſpeach moſt beautiful shal be confirmed of him. <na>[1]</na>

He that purſueth auarice diſturbeth his houſe: but he that hateth giftes shal liue. <na>[1]</na> By mercie and faith ſinnes are purged: and by the feare of our Lord euerie one declineth from euil. <na>[2]</na>
The minde of the iuſt meditateth obedience: the mouth of the impious redoundeth with euils. <na>[1]</na>
Our Lord is far from the impious: and he wil heare the prayers of the iuſt. <na>[1]</na>
The light of the eies reioyceth the ſoule: a good name fatteth the bones. <na>[1]</na>
The eare that heareth the reprehenſions of life, shal abide in the middes of the wiſe. <na>[1]</na>
He that reiecteth diſcipline, deſpiſeth his ſoule: but he that yeldeth to reprehenſions, is a poſſeſſour of the hart. <na>[1]</na>
The feare of our Lord, the diſcipline of wiſdom: and humilitie goeth before glorie. <na>[1]</na>
IT perteyneth to man to prepare the hart: and to our Lord to gouerne the tongue. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Gods grace neceſſarie in euerie good action.

verses.text: Al the wayes of man are open to his eies: our Lord is the weigher of ſpirites. <na>[1]</na>
Reueale thy workes to our Lord: and thy cogitations shal be directed. <na>[1]</na>
Our Lord hath wrought al thinges for himſelf: the impious alſo to the euil day. <na>[1]</na>

Euerie arrogant man is an abomination to our Lord: although hand shal be to hand he is not <na>[1]</na> innocent. <na>[2]</na> The beginning of a good way, is to doe iuſtice: and it is more acceptable with God, then to immolate hoſtes. <na>[3]</na>
By mercie and truth iniquitie is redemed: and in the feare of our Lord euil is auoided. <na>[1]</na>
When the wayes of man shal pleaſe our Lord, he wil conuert alſo his enemies to peace. <na>[1]</na>
Better is a litle with iuſtice, then much fruite with iniquitie. <na>[1]</na>
The hart of man diſpoſeth his way: but it perteyneth to our Lord to direct his progreſſe. <na>[1]</na>
<na>[1]</na> Diuination is in the lippes of the king, his mouth shal not erre in iudgement.

notes.text: God aſſiſteth ſuperiors in gouerning their ſubiectes.

verses.text: Weight and balance are iudgements of our Lord: and his worke al the ſtones of the bagge. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Iuſt balance do pleaſe God & good kinges.

verses.text: They are abominable to the king that doe impiously: becauſe the throne is eſtablished by iuſtice. <na>[1]</na>
The wil of kinges are iuſt lippes: he that ſpeaketh right thinges shal be beloued. <na>[1]</na>
The kings indignation, meſſengers of death: and the wiſe man wil pacifie it. <na>[1]</na>
In the cherfulnes of the kings countenance is life: and his clemencie is as the later showre.
Poſſeſſe wiſdom, becauſe it is better then gold: and gette prudence, becauſe it is more precious then ſiluer. <na>[1]</na>
The path of the iuſt auoideth euils: the keper of his ſoule kepeth his way. <na>[1]</na>
Pride goeth before deſtruction, and before ruine the ſpirit shal be exalted. <na>[1]</na>
It is better to be humbled with the meeke, then to diuide ſpoyles with the proude. <na>[1]</na>
The lerned in word shal finde good thinges: and he that hopeth in our Lord, is bleſſed. <na>[1]</na>
He that is wiſe in hart, shal be called prudent: and he that is ſweete in ſpeach shal finde greater thinges. <na>[1]</na>
A fountaine of life the lerning of him that poſſeſſeth it: the doctrine of fooles foolishnes. <na>[1]</na>
The hart of the wiſe shal inſtruct his mouth: and shal adde grace to his lippes. <na>[1]</na>
Wel ſet wordes are a honie combe: ſwetnes of the ſoule the health of the bones. <na>[1]</na>
There is a way that ſeemeth to a man right: and the later endes therof lead to death. <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na>
The ſoule of him that laboureth doth labour to himſelf, becauſe his mouth hath compelled him: <na>[1]</na>
The impious man diggeth euil, and in his lippes fire burneth. <na>[1]</na>
A peruerſe man raiſeth contentions: and one ful of wordes ſeparateth princes. <na>[1]</na>
An vniuſt man allureth his frende: and leadeth him by a way not good. <na>[1]</na>
He that with aſtoinied eies thinketh wicked thinges, byting his lippes bringeth euil to paſſe. <na>[1]</na>
A crowne of dignitie old age, which shal be found in the wayes of iuſtice. <na>[1]</na>
Better is the patient then a ſtrong man: and he that ruleth his minde, then the ouerthrower of cities. <na>[1]</na>
Lottes are caſt into the boſome, but they are ordered of our Lord. <na>[1]</na>
BEtter is a drie morſel with ioy, then a houſe ful of victimes with brawling. <na>[1]</na>
A wiſe ſeruant shal rule ouer foolish children, and diuide inheritance among bretheren. <na>[1]</na>
As ſiluer is tried by fyre, and gold in the fournace: ſo our Lord proueth the the harts. <na>[1]</na>
The euil man obeyeth an vniuſt tongue: and the deceitful obeyeth lying lippes. <na>[1]</na>
He that deſpiſeth the poore, vpbraydeth his maker: and he that reioyceth at an other mans ruine, shal not be vnpunished. <na>[1]</na>
The crowne of oldmen the childrens children: and the glorie of children their fathers. <na>[1]</na>
Eloquent wordes become not a foole, nor lying lippes a prince. <na>[1]</na>
A moſt gratful pearle, the expectation of him that expecteth: whither ſoeuer he turneth himſelf, he vnderſtandeth wiſely. <na>[1]</na>
He that concealeth offence, ſeeketh frendshipes: he that in other word repeteth it, ſeperateth the confederate. <na>[1]</na>
Reprehenſion doth more profit with a wiſeman, then an hundred ſtripes with a foole. <na>[1]</na>
An euil man alwayes ſeeketh brawles: but a cruel angel shal be ſent againſt him. <na>[1]</na>
It is better to meete a beare when her yong are taken away, then a foole truſting to himſelfe in his owne follie. <na>[1]</na>
He that rendereth euil thinges for good, euil shal not depart from his houſe. <na>[1]</na>
He that letteth water goe, is the head of brawles: & before he ſuffer contumelie, he forſaketh iudgement. <na>[1]</na>
He that iuſtifieth the impious, and he that condemneth the iuſt, both are abominable before God. <na>[1]</na>
What doth it profit a foole to haue riches, wheras he can not buy wiſdom? <na>[1]</na> He that maketh his houſe high, ſeeketh ruine: and he that refuſeth to learne, shal fal into euils. <na>[2]</na>
He loueth at al time that is a frend: and a brother is proued in diſtreſſes. <na>[1]</na>
A foolish man wil clappe the handes, when he is ſuretie for his freind. <na>[1]</na>
He that meditateth diſcordes, loueth brawles: and he that exalteth the doore, ſeeketh ruine. <na>[1]</na>
He that is of a peruerſe hart, shal not finde good: and he that turneth his tongue, shal fal into euil. <na>[1]</na>
A foole is borne to his owne ignominie: but neither shal the father reioyce in a foole. <na>[1]</na>
A ioyful minde maketh a florishing age: a ſorowful ſpirit dryeth vp the bones. <na>[1]</na>
The impious receiueth giftes out of the boſome, that he may peruert the pathes of iudgement. <na>[1]</na>
In the face of the prudent wiſdom shineth: the eies of fooles are in the endes of the earth. <na>[1]</na>
A foolish ſonne is the anger of the father: and the ſorow of the mother that bare him. <na>[1]</na>
It is not good, to doe hurt to the iuſt: nor to ſtrike the prince, which iudgeth right. <na>[1]</na>
He that moderateth his wordes, is lerned and prudent: and the lerned man is of a precious ſpirit. <na>[1]</na>
The foole alſo if he hold his peace, shal be reputed wiſe: and if he cloſe his lippes, a man of vnderſtanding. <na>[1]</na>
HE ſeeketh occaſions that wil depart from a frend: he shal euer be ſubiect to reproch. <na>[1]</na>
A foole receiueth not the wordes of prudence: vnleſſe thou ſay thoſe thinges which are in his hart. <na>[1]</na>
The impious when he shal come into the depth of ſinnes, contemneth: but ignominie and reproch folow him. <na>[1]</na>
Deepe water wordes from the mouth of a <na>[1]</na> man: and a ſtreame ouerflowing the fountaine of wiſdom. <na>[2]</na>
To accept the perſon of the impious in iudgement is not good, that thou decline from the truth of iudgement. <na>[1]</na>
The lippes of a foole mingle him with ſtrife: and his mouth prouoketh brawles. <na>[1]</na>
The mouth of a foole is his deſtruction: and his lippes are the ruine of his ſoule. <na>[1]</na>

The wordes of the duble tongued, as it were ſimple: and the ſame come euen to the inner part of the bellie. <na>[1]</na> Feare caſteth downe the ſlothful: and the ſoules of the effeminate shal be hungrie. <na>[2]</na>
He that is ſoft and diſſolute in his worke, is the brother of him that deſtroyeth his owne workes. <na>[1]</na>
A moſt ſtrong towre, the name of our Lord: the iuſt runneth to it, and shal be exalted. <na>[1]</na>
The ſubſtance of the rich man a citie of his ſtrength: and as a ſtrong wal compaſſing him about. <na>[1]</na>
Before he be broken, the hart of a man is exalted: and before he be glorified, it is humbled. <na>[1]</na>
He that anſwereth before he heare, sheweth him ſelf to be a foole, and worthie of confuſion. <na>[1]</na>
The ſpirit of a man vpholdeth his imbecilitie: but a ſpirit that is eaſie to be angrie who can ſuſteyne? <na>[1]</na>
A wiſe hart shal poſſeſſe knowlege: and the eare of the wiſe ſeeketh doctrine. <na>[1]</na>
The gift of a man enlargeth his way, & maketh him roome before princes. <na>[1]</na>
The iuſt is firſt accuſer of himſelf: his frend commeth, and shal ſearch him. <na>[1]</na>
Lotte ſuppreſſeth contradictions, and betwen the mightie alſo it determineth. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Vſe of lote to make agreement.

verses.text: Brother that is holpen of brother, is as a ſtrong citie: and iudgements are as the barres of cities. <na>[1]</na>
Of the fruite of mans mouth his bellie shal be filled: and the offſprings of his lippes shal fil him. <na>[1]</na>
Death and life in the hand of the tongue: they that loue it, shal eate the fruites therof. <na>[1]</na>
He that hath found a good wife, hath found a good thing, and hath receiued a pleaſure of our Lord. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: A wiues vertue is her beſt dowrie.

verses.text: The poore ſpeaketh with ſupplications, and the rich wil ſpeake roughly. <na>[1]</na>
A man amiable to ſocietie, shal be more frendlie, then a brother. <na>[1]</na>
BEtter is a poore man, that walketh in his ſimplicitie, then a rich writhing his lippes, and vnwiſe. <na>[1]</na>
Where is no knowlege of the ſoule, is not good: and he that is haſtie with his feete shal ſtumble. <na>[1]</na>
The follie of a man ſupplanteth his ſteppes: and he boileth in his minde againſt God. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Mans owne wil the cauſe of euil.

verses.text: Riches adde manie frendes: but from the poore they alſo which he had are ſeparated. <na>[1]</na>
A falſe witnes shal not be vnpunished:& he that ſpeaketh lies, shal not eſcape. <na>[1]</na>
Manie worshipe the perſon of the mightie, and are frendes of him that geueth giftes. <na>[1]</na>
The brethren of the poore man hate him:more ouer alſo his frendes haue departed far from him. <na>[1]</na>
He that purseweth wordes only, shal haue nothing: but he that is poſſeſſour of the minde, loueth his ſoule, and the keper of prudence shal finde good thinges. <na>[1]</na>
A falſe witneſſe shal not be vnpunished: and he that ſpeaketh lies shal perish. <na>[1]</na>
Delicacies become not a foole: nor a ſeruant to rule ouer princes. <na>[1]</na>
The doctrine of man is knowen by patience: and his glorie is to ouerpaſſe vniuſt thinges. <na>[1]</na>
As the roaring of a lion, ſo alſo the anger of a king: and as dew vpon graſſe, ſo alſo his cherefulnes. <na>[1]</na>
The ſorow of the father, a foolish ſonne: and roofes continually dropping through, a woman ful of brawling. <na>[1]</na>
Houſe and riches are geuen of the parents: but of our Lord properly a prudent wife. <na>[1]</na>
Slothfulneſſe bringeth drouſineſſe, and a diſſolute ſoule shal be an hungred. <na>[1]</na>
He that kepeth the commandement, kepeth his ſoule: but he that neglecteth his way, shal die. <na>[1]</na>
He lendeth our Lord that hath mercie on the poore: and he wil repay him the like. <na>[1]</na>
Nurter thy ſonne, deſpayre not: but to the killing of him ſet not thy ſoule. <na>[1]</na>
He that is impatient, shal ſuſteyne damage: and when he shal take away violently, he shal adde an other thing. <na>[1]</na>
Heare counſel, and receiue diſcipline, that thou mayſt be wiſe in thy later endes. <na>[1]</na>
Manie cogitations in the hart of a man: but the wil of our Lord shal be permanent. <na>[1]</na>
A needie man is merciful: and better is the poore then the lying man. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Good wil to helpe the poore.

verses.text: The feare of our Lord vnto life: and in fulnes he shal abide, without the viſitation moſt noyſome. <na>[1]</na>
The ſlothful hideth his hand vnder the armehole, neither doth he put it to his mouth. <na>[1]</na>
The peſtilent man being whipped, the foole shal be wiſer: but if thou rebuke a wiſeman he wil vnderſtand diſcipline. <na>[1]</na>
He that afflicteth his father, and fleeth from his mother, is ignominious and vnhappie. <na>[1]</na>
Ceaſe not ô ſonne to heare doctrine, neither be ignorant of the wordes of knowlege. <na>[1]</na>
An vniuſt witnes ſcorneth iudgement: and the mouth of the impious deuoureth iniquitie. <na>[1]</na>
Iudgements are prepared for ſcorners: & hammers ſtriking for the bodies of fooles. <na>[1]</na>
VVIne is a luxurious thing, & drunkenes tumultuous: whoſoeuer is delighted therwith shal not be wiſe. <na>[1]</na>
As the roaring of a lyon, ſo alſo the terrour of a king: he that prouoketh him, ſinneth alſo againſt his owne ſoule. <na>[1]</na>
It is honour to a man, that ſeparateth himſelf from contentions: but al fooles medle with contumelies. <na>[1]</na>
Becauſe of cold the slothful would not plowe: he shal begge therfore in the ſummer, and it shal not be geuen him. <na>[1]</na>
As deepe water, ſo counſel in the hart of a man: but a wiſe man shal draw it out. <na>[1]</na>
Manie men are called merciful: but a faithful man who shal fynd? <na>[1]</na>
The iuſt that walketh in his ſimplicitie, shal leaue bleſſed children. <na>[1]</na>
The king, that ſitteth in the throne of iudgement, diſſipateth al euil with his looke. <na>[1]</na>
Who can ſay: My hart is cleane, I am pure from ſinne? <na>[1]</na>
Weight and weight, meaſure and meaſure: both are abominable before God. <na>[1]</na>
By his conuerſation a child is perceiued, if his workes be cleane and right. <na>[1]</na>
The eare hearing, and the eie ſeing, our Lord made both. <na>[1]</na>
Loue not ſleepe, leſt pouertie oppreſſe thee: open thyne eies and be filled with breades. <na>[1]</na>
It is naught, it is naught, ſayth euerie byer: and when he is departed he wil boaſt. <na>[1]</na>
There is gold, and multitude of pearles: but a precious veſſel the lippes of knowlege. <na>[1]</na>
Take his garment, that was the ſuretie of a ſtranger, and for ſtrangers take a pledge from him. <na>[1]</na>
The bread of lying is ſwete to a man: and afterward his mouth shal be filled with the grauelſtone. <na>[1]</na>
Cogitations are ſtrengthened by counſels: and battels are to be handled by gouernmentes. <na>[1]</na>
Medle not with him that reuealeth myſteries, and walketh fraudulently, and dilateth his lippes. <na>[1]</na>
He that curſeth his father, and mother, his lampe shal be extinquished in the middes of darkenes. <na>[1]</na>
The inheritance wherunto haſte is made in the beginning, in the later end shal lacke bleſſing. <na>[1]</na>
Say not: I wil requit euil: expect our Lord, and he wil deliuer thee. <na>[1]</na>
Weight and weight are abomination with our Lord: a deceitful balance is not good. <na>[1]</na>
The ſteppes of man are directed of our Lord: but who of men can vnderſtand his owne way? <na>[1]</na>
It is ruine to a man, to deuoure ſaintes, and afterward to retracte the vowes. <na>[1]</na>
A wiſe king diſſipateth the impious, and bendeth ouer them a triumphant arch. <na>[1]</na>
The lampe of our Lord, the breath of a man, which ſearcheth al the ſecretes of the bellie. <na>[1]</na>
Mercie, & truth kepe the king, and his throne is ſtrengthened by clemencie. <na>[1]</na>
The ioy of yongmen their ſtrength: and the dignitie of oldmen a gray head. <na>[1]</na>
The blewneſſe of the wound shal wipe away euils: and ſtripes in the more ſecrete place of the bellie. <na>[1]</na>
AS diuiſions of waters, ſo the hart of the king is in the hand of our Lord: whither ſoeuer he wil, he shal incline it. <na>[1]</na>
Euerie way of a man ſemeth to himſelf right: but our Lord weigheth the hartes. <na>[1]</na>
To doe mercie and iudgement, doth more pleaſe our Lord, then victimes. <na>[1]</na>
Exaltation of the eies is the dilatation of the hart: the lampe of the impious ſinne. <na>[1]</na>
The cogitations of the ſtrong are alwayes in abundance: but euerie ſluggard is alwayes in pouertie. <na>[1]</na>
He that gathereth treaſures with a lying tongue, is vaine and witles, and shal ſtumble at the ſnares of death. <na>[1]</na>
The robberies of the impious, shal draw them downe, becauſe they would not doe iudgement. <na>[1]</na>
The peruerſe way of a man is ſtrange: but he that is cleane, his worke is right. <na>[1]</na>
It is better to ſitte in a corner of the houſe toppe, then with a brawling woman, and in a common houſe. <na>[1]</na>
The ſoule of the impious deſireth euil, he wil not haue pitie on his neighbour. <na>[1]</na>
The peſtilent man being punished, the litle one wil be wiſer: and if he folow the wiſeman, he wil take knowlege. <na>[1]</na>
The iuſt deuiſeth concerning the houſe of the impious, that he may draw the impious from euil. <na>[1]</na>
He that ſtoppeth his eare at the crie of the poore, himſelf alſo shal crie, and shal not be heard. <na>[1]</na>
A gift hid quencketh angers: and a gift in the boſome the greateſt indignation. <na>[1]</na>
It is a ioy to the iuſt to doe iudgement: and dread to them that worke iniquitie. <na>[1]</na>
A man, that shal erre from the way of doctrine, shal abyde in the aſſemblie of giantes. <na>[1]</na>
He that loueth good cheere, shal be in pouertie: he that loueth wine, and fatte thinges, shal not be rich. <na>[1]</na>
The impious shal be geuen for the iuſt: and the vniuſt for the righteous. <na>[1]</na>
It is better to dwel in a deſert land, then with a brawling and angrie woman. <na>[1]</na>
Treaſure to be deſired, and oyle in the habitation of the iuſt: and the vnwiſe man shal diſſipate it. <na>[1]</na>
He that foloweth iuſtice and mercie, shal finde life, iuſtice, and glorie. <na>[1]</na>
The wiſe hath ſcaled the citie of the ſtrong, and hath deſtroyed the confidence therof. <na>[1]</na>
He that kepeth his mouth, and his tongue, kepeth his ſoule from diſtreſſes. <na>[1]</na>
The proude and arrogant is called vnlerned, which in anger worketh pride. <na>[1]</na>
Deſires kil the ſlothful: for his handes would not worke any thing: <na>[1]</na>
al the day he longeth and deſireth: but he that is iuſt, wil geue, and wil not ceaſe. <na>[1]</na>
The hoſtes of the impious abominable, becauſe they are offered of wickednes. <na>[1]</na>
A lying witnes shal perish: an obedient man shal ſpeake victorie. <na>[1]</na>
The impious man malepertly hardeneth his countenance: but he that is righteous, correcteth his way. <na>[1]</na>
There is no wiſdom, there is no prudence, there is no counſel againſt our Lord. <na>[1]</na>
The horſe is prepared to the day of battel: but our Lord geueth ſaluation. <na>[1]</na>
BEtter is a good name, then much riches: aboue ſiluer and gold, good grace. <na>[1]</na>
The rich and poore haue mette one an other: our Lord is the maker of both. <na>[1]</na>
The ſubtel saw euil, and hyd himſelf: the innocent paſſed by, and was afflicted with damage. <na>[1]</na>
The end of modeſtie the feare of our Lord, riches and glorie and life. <na>[1]</na>
Armour and ſwordes in the way of the peruerſe: but the keper of his owne ſoule departeth far from them. <na>[1]</na>
It is a prouerbe: A yongman according to his way, when he is old, wil not depart from it. <na>[1]</na>
The richman ruleth ouer the poore: and he that boroweth is the ſeruant of him that lendeth. <na>[1]</na>
He that ſoweth iniquitie, shal reape euils, and with the rod of his wrath, he shal be conſumed. <na>[1]</na>

He that is prone to mercie, shal be bleſſed: for of his breades he hath geuen to the poore. <na>[1]</na> He that geueth giftes shal purchaſe victorie and honour: but he that receiueth taketh away the ſoule of the geuer. <na>[2]</na>

notes.text: Better to geue then to take.

verses.text: Caſt out the ſcorner, and brawling shal goe forth with him, and cauſe shal ceaſe and contumelies. <na>[1]</na>
He that loueth cleanes of hart, for the grace of his lippes, shal haue the king his frend. <na>[1]</na>
The eies of our Lord keepe knowlege: and the wordes of the iuſt are ſupplanted. <na>[1]</na>
The ſlothful ſayth: A lyon is without, in the middes of the ſtreates I am to be ſlayne. <na>[1]</na>
A deepe pitte the mouth of a ſtrange woman: he with whom our Lord is angrie, shal fal into it. <na>[1]</na>
Follie is tyed together in the hart of a childe, and the rod of diſcipline shal driue it away. <na>[1]</na>
He that doth calumniate the poore, to increaſe his riches, himſelf shal geue to a richer, and shal be in neede. <na>[1]</na>
Incline thine eare, and heare the wordes of wiſemen: and ſet thy hart to my doctrine: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Rules of wiſdom are neceſſarie, profitable, and vpon practiſe found pleaſant: rightly directing al our thougtes wordes and dedes.

verses.text: which shal be beautiful for thee, when thou shalt kepe it in thy bellie, and it shal flow in thy lippes.
That thy confidence may be in our Lord, wherfore I haue shewed alſo it to thee this day.
Behold I haue deſcribed it to thee three maner of wayes, in cogitations and knowledge:
that I might shew thee the ſtabilitie, and the wordes of truth, out of theſe to anſwer them, that ſent thee.
Doe not violence to the poore, becauſe he is poore: neither oppreſſe the needie in the gate: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Care of the poore, becauſe they are deare to God.

verses.text: becauſe our Lord wil iudge his cauſe, and wil pearſe them, that haue pearſed his ſoule.
Be not frend to an angrie man, nor walke with a furious man: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Flee from euil companie which may corrupt thee.

verses.text: leſt perhaps thou lerne his pathes, and take ſcandal to thy ſoule.
Be not with them, that ſticke downe their handes, and that offer themſelues ſureties for debts: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Auoide ſuretishipe, leſt thou fal into diſtreſſe.

verses.text: for if thou haue not wherewith to reſtore, what cauſe is there, that he should take the couering from thy bed?
Trangreſſe not the ancient boundes, which thy fathers haue put. <na>[1]</na>
Haſt thou ſene a man quicke in his worke? he shal ſtand before kinges, neither shal be before the vnnoble. <na>[1]</na>
VVHEN thou shalt ſitte to eate with a prince, attend diligently what thinges are ſet before thy face: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Modeſtie and diſcretion at the table of great perſons.

verses.text: and ſet a knife in thy throte, if notwithſtanding thou haue thy ſoule in thine owne power.
Deſire not his meates, in which is the bread of lying.
