Labour not to be rich: but ſet a meane to thy prudence. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Mediocritie of riches, and contentment with meane ſtate.

verses.text: Lift not vp thine eies to the riches, which thou canſt not haue: becauſe they shal make to themſelues winges as of an eagle, and shal flie into heauen.
Eate not with an enuious man, and deſire not his meates. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Eate not with a niggard, leſt he be ſecretly greued, outwardly diſſembling, and thyſelf repent it.

verses.text: Becauſe after the ſimilitude of a ſouthſayer, and diuiner, he eſteemeth that which he knoweth not. Eate and drinke, wil he ſay to thee: and his minde is not with thee.
The meates which thou hadſt eaten thou shalt vomite vp: and shalt loſe thy beautiful wordes.
Speake not in the eares of the vnwiſe: becauſe they wil deſpiſe the doctrine of thy ſpeach. <na>[1]</na>
Touch not the boundes of litle ones: and into the filde of pupils enter not. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Hurt not orphanes: for they are deare to God.

verses.text: For their nerekinsman is ſtrong: and he wil iudge their cauſe againſt thee.
Let thy hart enter into doctrin: and thyne eares to wordes of knowlege. <na>[1]</na>
Withdrawe not diſcipline from a childe: for if thou shalt ſtrike him with the rod, he shal not die. <na>[1]</na>
Thou shalt ſtrike him with the rod: and deliuer his ſoule from hel.
My ſonne, if thy minde shal be wiſe, my hart shal be glad with thee: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Vertues of children are ioyful to the parentes.

verses.text: And my reines shal reioyce, when thy lippes shal ſpeake right thinges.
Let not thy hart enuie ſinners: but in the feare of our Lord be thou al the day: <na>[1]</na>
becauſe thou shalt haue hope in the later end, and thyn exaltation shal not be taken away. <na>[1]</na>
Heare my ſonne, & be wiſe: & direct thy minde in the way. <na>[1]</na>
Be not in the feaſtes of great drinkers, nor in their comeſſations, which contribute flesh together to eate:
becauſe they that are geuen to drinking, and that pay shottes, shal be conſumed, and drouſines shal be clothed with ragges. <na>[1]</na>
Heare thy father, that begot thee: and contemne not thy mother when she is old. <na>[1]</na>
Bye truth, and ſel not wiſedom, and doctrine, and intelligence. <na>[1]</na>
The father of the iuſt reioyceth with gladnes: he that hath begotten a wiſeman, shal reioyce in him. <na>[1]</na>
Let thy father be glad, and thy mother, and let her reioyce that bare thee.
My ſonne geue me thy hart: & let thyne eies kepe my wayes. <na>[1]</na>
For an harlot is a deepe dich: & a ſtrange woman a narrow pitte.
She lyeth in wayt in the way as a robber, and whom she shal ſee not circumſpect, she wil kil.
To whom is woe? to whoſe father woe? to whom browles? to whom diches? to whom woundes without cauſe? to whom bloud sheeding eies? <na>[1]</na>
Is it not to them that paſſe their time in wine, and ſtudie to drinke out their cuppes?
Behold not wine when it waxeth yelow, when the colour therof shal shine in the glaſſe: it goeth in pleaſantly, <na>[1]</na>
but in the end, it wil bite like a ſnake, and as a baſiliske it wil powre abrode poyſones. <na>[1]</na>
Thine eies shal ſee ſtrange wemen, and thy hart shal ſpeake peruerſe thinges. <na>[1]</na>
And thou shalt be as one ſleeping in the middes of the ſea, and as the gouernour faſt a ſleepe, the ſterne being loſt. <na>[1]</na>
And thou shalt ſay: They haue beaten me, but I was not greeued: they drew me, and I felt not: When shal I awake, and finde wines againe? <na>[1]</na>
EMVLATE not euil men, neither deſire thou to be with them: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Flee euil companie, leſt thou be alured to vice.

verses.text: becauſe their mind doth meditate robberies, and their lippes ſpeake deceites.
By wiſedom the houſe shal be built, and by prudence it shal be ſtrengthened. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: VViſdom and vertues, not wickednes, do proſper temporally and ſpiritualy.

verses.text: In doctrine the cellars shal be replenished with al precious, and moſt beautiful ſubſtance.
A wiſeman is ſtrong: and a lerned man, ſtrong and valiant.
Becauſe warre is managed by due ordering & there shal be ſaluation where manie counſels are. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Counſel in warres, and other great affayres.

verses.text: Wiſedom is high for a foole, in the gate he shal not open his mouth.
He that thinketh to doe euils, shal be called a foole. <na>[1]</na>
The cogitation of a foole is ſinne: and a detracter the abomination of men. <na>[1]</na>
If thou deſpaire being wearie in the day of diſtreſſe: thy ſtrength shal be diminished. <na>[1]</na>
Deliuer them that are led to death: and thoſe that are drawen to death ceaſe not to deliuer. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: VVorkes of mercie, according to our habilitie.

verses.text: If thou ſay: I am not of force: he that ſeeth into the hart, he vnderſtandeth, and nothing deceiueth the keeper of thy ſoule, and he shal render to a man according to his workes.
Eate honie my ſonne, becauſe it is good, and the honie-combe moſt ſweete to thy throte: <na>[1]</na>
ſo alſo the doctrine of wiſedom to thy ſoule: which when thou shalt finde, thou shalt haue hope in the later end, and thy hope shal not perish. <na>[1]</na>
Lie not in wayte, nor ſeeke impietie in the houſe of the iuſt, nor ſpoile his reſt. <na>[1]</na>
For ſeuen <na>[1]</na> times shal the iuſt fal, and shal riſe againe: but the impious shal fal into euil. <na>[2]</na>
When thine enemie shal fal, be not glad, and in his ruine let not thy hart reioyce: <na>[1]</na>
Leſt perhaps our Lord ſee, and it diſpleaſe him, and he take away his wrath from him.
Contend not with the moſt wicked, nor emulate the impious: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Haue peace with al: ſo much as may be.

verses.text: becauſe euil men haue not hope of thinges to come, and the lampe of the impious shal be extinguished.
Feare our Lord, my ſonne, and the king: & with detracters medle not: <na>[1]</na>
becauſe their perdition shal ſodenly riſe: and the ruine of both who knoweth?
Theſe thinges alſo to the wiſe: to know a perſon in iudgement is not good. <na>[1]</na>
They that ſay to the impious: Thou art iuſt: peoples shal curſe them, and tribes shal deteſt them. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Equitie in iudgement, condemning the guiltie, & deliuering the innocent, is very gratful to al.

verses.text: They that rebuke him, shal be prayſed: and bleſſing shal come vpon them.
He shal kiſſe the lippes, who anſwereth right wordes.
Prepare thy worke abrode, and diligently til thy ground: that afterward thou mayſt build thy houſe. <na>[1]</na>
Be not witnes without cauſe againſt thy neighbour: neither alure any man with thy lippes. <na>[1]</na>
Say not: As he hath done to me, ſo wil I doe to him: I wil render to euerie one according to his worke. <na>[1]</na>
I paſſed by the filde of a ſlothful man, and by the vineyard of a foolish man: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Diligent labour, and vigilance to prouide neceſſaries, and to auoide beggerie.

verses.text: and behold nettels had filled it wholy, and thornes had couered the face therof, and the wal of ſtones was deſtroyed.
Which when I had ſeene, I layd it in my hart, and by the example I lerned diſcipline.
A litle I ſay, thou shalt ſleepe, a litle thou shalt ſlumber, a litle shalt thou ioyne thy handes together, to reſt:
and as a poſte, pouertie shal come to thee, & beggerie as a man armed.
THeſe <na>[1]</na> alſo are the parables of Salomon, which the men of Ezechias king of Iuda wrote out.

notes.text: The 2. part. More Parables of Salomon written by others.

verses.text: It is the glorie of God to conceale the word, and the glorie of kinges to ſearch the ſpeach. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Gods workes are not al reueled.

verses.text: The heauen aboue, and the earth beneth, and the hart of kinges is vnſcrutable. <na>[1]</na>
Take away the ruſt from ſiluer, and there shal comeforth a moſt pure veſſel:
Take away impietie from the kings countenance, and his throne shal be eſtablished with iuſtice. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Publique iuſtice and punishment of ſinne.

verses.text: Appeare not glorious before the king, and in the place of great men ſtand not. <na>[1]</na>
For it is better that it be ſaid to thee: Come vp hither; then that thou be humbled before the prince. <na>[1]</na>
The thinges which thy eies haue ſene, vtter not quickly in a brawle: leſt afterward thou canſt not amend it, when thou haſt dishonoured thy frend. <na>[1]</na>
Treate thy cauſe with thy frend, and reueale not a ſecret to a ſtranger: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Compoſe controuerſies ſecretly, rather then contend in publique court.

verses.text: leſt perhaps he inſult againſt thee, when he heareth, and ceaſe not to vpbraide thee. Grace and frendshipe deliuer: <na>[1]</na> which kepe to thyſelf, leſt thou become reprochful.
Apples of gold in ſiluer beddes, he that ſpeaketh a word in his time. <na>[1]</na>
A golden earlet, and a shining precious ſtone, he that rebuketh a wiſeman, and an obedient eare. <na>[1]</na>
As the cold of ſnow in the day of harueſt, ſo a faithful legate to him, that ſent him, maketh his ſoule to reſt. <na>[1]</na>
Cloudes, and winde, and no rayne folowing, a glorious man, and not accomplishing his promiſes. <na>[1]</na>
By patience the prince shal be pacified, and a ſoft tongue shal breake hardnes. <na>[1]</na>
Thou haſt found honie, eate that which ſufficeth thee, leſt perhaps being filled thou vomite it vp. <na>[1]</na>
Withdraw thy foote from the houſe of thy neighbour, leſt ſome time hauing his fil he hate thee. <na>[1]</na>
A dart, and ſword, and a sharpe arrow, a man that ſpeaketh falſe teſtimonie againſt his neighbour. <na>[1]</na>
A rotten tooth, and wearie foote, he that hopeth vpon the vnfaithful in the day of diſtreſſe, <na>[1]</na>

and that loſeth his cloke in the day of cold. Vineger in <na>[1]</na> nither, he that ſingeth ſonges to a naughtie hart. <na>[2]</na> As a moth the garment, and a worme the woode: ſo the ſadnes of a man hurteth the hart. <na>[3]</na>
If thine enemie shal hunger, geue him meate: if he thirſt, geue him water to drinke: <na>[1]</na>
for thou shalt heape hote coales vpon his head, and our Lord wil reward thee. <cr>[1]</cr>
The northwinde diſſipateth raynes, & a ſad looke the tongue that detracteth. <na>[1]</na>
It is better to ſitte in a corner of the houſe toppe, then with a brawling woman, and in a common houſe. <na>[1]</na>
Cold water to a thirſtie ſoule, and good tydings from a far countrie. <na>[1]</na>
A fountaine trubled with the foote, and a vaine corrupted, the iuſt falling before the impious. <na>[1]</na>
As he that eateth much honie, it is not good for him: ſo he that is a ſearcher of the maieſtie, shal be oppreſſed of the glorie. <na>[1]</na>
As a citie being open and without compaſſe of walles, ſo a man that can not repreſſe his ſpirit in ſpeaking. <na>[1]</na>
AS ſnow in the ſummer, and rayne in the harueſt: ſo is glorie vndecent for a foole. <na>[1]</na>
As a birde flying to other places, & a ſparow going whither he liſt: ſo a curſe vttered in vaine shal light vpon ſome man. <na>[1]</na>
A whippe for a horſe, and a ſnaffle for an aſſe, and a rod on the back of the vnwiſe. <na>[1]</na>
Anſwer not a foole according to his follie, leſt thou be made like to him. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Anſwer a foole wiſely: detecting his follie.

verses.text: Anſwer a foole according to his follie, leſt he ſeme to himſelf to be wiſe.
Lame of feete, and drinking iniquitie, he that ſendeth wordes by a foolish meſſenger. <na>[1]</na>
As a lame man hath fayre legges in vaine: ſo a parable is vndecent in the mouth of fooles. <na>[1]</na>
As he that caſteth a ſtone into the heape of Mercurie: ſo he that geueth honour to the vnwiſe. <na>[1]</na>
As if a thorne should grow in the hand of the drunkard: ſo a parable in the mouth of fooles. <na>[1]</na>
Iudgement determineth cauſes: and he that putteth a foole to ſilence, apeaſeth angers. <na>[1]</na>
As a dog that returneth to his vomite, ſo the vnwiſe that reiterateth his follie. <na>[1]</na>
Haſt thou ſene a man ſeeme to himſelfe wiſe? the foole shal haue hope rather then he. <na>[1]</na>
The ſlothful ſayth: A lyon is in the way, and a lyoneſſe in the iourneis: <na>[1]</na>
as a doore turneth on his hinge ſo the ſlothful in his bed. <na>[1]</na>
The ſlothful hideth his hand vnder the armehole, and is greeued if he turneth it to his mouth. <na>[1]</na>
The ſlothful ſeemeth wiſer to himſelfe, then ſeuen men ſpeaking ſentences. <na>[1]</na>
As he that taketh a dog by the eares, ſo he that paſſeth by impatient, and medleth with an other mans brawle. <na>[1]</na>
As he is hurtful that shooteth arrowes, and ſpeares vnto death:
ſo a man, that hurteth his frende fraudulently: and when he is taken with al ſayth: I did it in ieſt. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Vnfained frendship, eſpecially in familiar acquaintance.

verses.text: When wood fayleth, the fire shal be extinguished: and the whiſperer taken away, brawles ceaſe. <na>[1]</na>
As coles to burning coles, and wood to fire, ſo an angrie man rayſeth brawles. <na>[1]</na>
The wordes of the whiſperer as it were ſimple, and the ſame come to the inmoſt partes of the bellie. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Heare not whiſperers of euil reportes.

verses.text: As if thou wouldeſt adorne an earthen veſſel with droſſie ſiluer, ſo ſwelling lippes ioyned with a moſt wicked hart. <na>[1]</na>
An enemie is perceiued by his lippes, when he shal handle deceites in his hart. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: VVhoſe flaterie and ſoft ſpeach are ſuſpicious, they wil fal at laſt into their owne trappes, truth preuailing.

verses.text: When he shal ſubmit his voyce, beleue him not: becauſe there are ſeuen miſchiefes in his hart.
He that couereth hatred fraudulently, his malice shal be reuealed in the councel.
He that diggeth a pit, shal fal into it: and he that rolleth a ſtone, it shal returne to him.
A deceitful tongue loueth not truth, and a ſlipper mouth worketh ruines.
BOaſt not for to morow, being ignorant what the day to come may bringforth. <na>[1]</na>
Let an other prayſe thee, and not thine owne mouth: a ſtranger and not thine owne lippes. <na>[1]</na>
A ſtone is heauie, and ſand weightie: but the anger of a foole is heauier then both. <na>[1]</na>
Anger hath no mercie, nor furie breaking forth: and the violence of a moued ſpirit who can ſuſteyne? <na>[1]</na>
Better is manifeſt correption, then loue hidden. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Loue friendly ſeueritie, not enemy's flaterie.

verses.text: Better are the woundes of him that loueth, then the fraudulent kiſſes of him that hateth.
A ſoule that is ful shal treade vpon the honiecombe: and a ſoule that is hungrie shal take bitter alſo for ſweete. <na>[1]</na>
As a bird fleeting from her neſt, ſo a man that forſaketh his place. <na>[1]</na>
The hart is delighted with oyntement and diuers odours: and with the good counſels of a frend the ſoule is ſweetned. <na>[1]</na>
Thy frend, and thy fathers frend do not leaue: and goe not into thy brothers houſe in the day of thyne affliction. Better is a neighbour neere thene a brother far of. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Old freindes are better, & ſurer then a kinſman.

verses.text: Studie wiſedom my ſonne, & make my hart ioyful, that thou maiſt make anſwer to the vpbrayder. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Be wiſe euen for thy fathers ſake.

verses.text: . The ſubtel man ſeeing euil, hideth himſelf: litle ones paſſing through haue ſuſteyned euil detriments.
Take his garment, that hath bene ſuretie for a ſtranger: and for alienes take from him a pledge. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Foreſee and preuent dangers. Truſt not enimies.

verses.text: He that bleſſeth his neighbour with a loud voice, riſing in the night, he shal be like him that curſeth. <na>[1]</na>
Dropping through in the day of cold, and a brawling woman are compared together: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Tolerate incorrigible brawlers with patience; leſt they become worſe, by thy ſtriuing to amend them.

verses.text: He that reteyneth her, as he that should hold the winde, and shal cal in the oyle of his right hand.
Iron is sharpened with iron, and a man sharpeneth the face of his frend.
He that kepeth the feegtree, shal eate the frute therof: and he that is the keper of his maſter, shal be glorified. <na>[1]</na>
As in waters the countenance of them that looke therin shyneth, ſo the hartes of men are manifeſt to the prudent. <na>[1]</na>
Hel and perdition are neuer filled: in like maner alſo the eies of men are vnſatiable. <na>[1]</na>

As ſiluer is tried in the forge, and gold in the fornace: ſo a man is proued by the mouth of him that praiſeth. <na>[1]</na> The hart of the wicked ſeeketh after euils, but the righteous hart ſeeketh after knowlege. <na>[2]</na>
If thou shalt bray a foole in a morter, as when a peſtle ſtriketh vpon ptiſane, his follie shal not be taken from him. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Striue not to teach a foole.

verses.text: Know diligently the countenance of thy cattel, and conſider thy flockes: <na>[1]</na>
For thou shalt not haue power alwayes: but a crowne shal be geuen into generation and generation. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: VVhiles thou art in this life.

verses.text: The medowes are open, and the grene herbes haue appeared, and the graſſe is gathered out of the mountaines.
Lambes for thy garment: and kiddes the price of the filde.
Let the milke of the goates ſuffice thee for thy meates, and for the neceſſities of thy houſe: and for victual to thy handmaides. <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na>

notes.text: Be content with things neceſſarie, and they shal be given to thee.

verses.text: THE impious fleeth, no man purſewing: but the iuſt confident as a lyon, shal be without terrour. <na>[1]</na>
For the ſinnes of the land the princes therof shal be manie: & for the wiſedom of a man, & the knowlege of thoſe thinges that are ſaid, the life of the prince shal be longer. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: General pietie of the people procureth Gods fauour.

verses.text: A poore man calumniating the poore, is like a vehement showre, wherby famine is gotten. <na>[1]</na>
They that forſake the lawe, praiſe the impious: they that kepe it, are ſet on fire againſt him. <na>[1]</na>
Euil men thinke not on iudgement: but they that ſeeke after our Lord, marke al thinges. <na>[1]</na>
Better is a poore man walking in his ſimplicitie, then the rich in crooked wayes. <na>[1]</na>
He that kepeth the law is a wiſe ſonne, but he that feedeth gluttons, shameth his father. <na>[1]</na>
He that heapeth together riches by vſuries and ocker, gathereth them for him that is liberal to the poore. <na>[1]</na>
He that turneth away his eares from hearing the law, his prayer shal be execrable. <na>[1]</na>
He that deceiueth the iuſt in a wicked way, shal fal into his deſtruction: and the ſimple shal poſſeſſe his goodes. <na>[1]</na>
The rich man ſeemeth to him ſelf wiſe: but the poore man being prudent shal ſearche him. <na>[1]</na>
In the exultation of the iuſt there is much glorie: when the impious reigne ruines of men. <na>[1]</na>
He that hideth his wicked deedes, shal not be directed: but he that shal confeſſe, and shal forſake them, shal obtayne mercie. <na>[1]</na>
Bleſſed is the man, that is alwayes fearful: but he that is of an obſtinate mynde, shal fal into euil. <na>[1]</na>
A roaring lyon, and hungrie beare, an impious prince ouer the poore people. <na>[1]</na>
A prince lacking prudence, shal oppreſſe many by calumnie: but he that hateth auarice, his dayes shal be made long. <na>[1]</na>
A man that doth calumniat the bloud of a ſoule, if he shal flee into a lake, no man abideth. <na>[1]</na>
He that walketh ſimply shal be ſaued: he that goeth peruerſe wayes, shal fal once. <na>[1]</na>
He that tilleth his ground, shal be filled with breads: but he that purſeweth idlneſſe, shal be replenished with pouertie. <na>[1]</na>
A faithful man shal be much prayſed: but he that haſteneth to be rich, shal not be innocent. <na>[1]</na>
He that knoweth a perſon in iudgement, doth not wel: this man euen for a morſel of bread forſaketh the truth. <na>[1]</na>
A man, that haſteneth to be rich, and enuyeth others, is ignorant that pouertie shal come vpon him. <na>[1]</na>
He that rebuketh a man, shal afterward find fauour with him more then he, that by flatteries of tongue deceiueth. <na>[1]</na>
He that pilfereth any thing from his father, and from his mother: & ſaith this is no ſinne, is the partaker of a mankiller. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: To robbe parents is a greuous crime.

verses.text: He that exulteth, and dilateth himſelfe, rayſeth brawles: but he that truſteth in our Lord, shal be healed. <na>[1]</na>
He that hath confidence in his owne hart, is a foole: but who ſo walketh wiſely shal be ſaued. <na>[1]</na>
He that geueth to the poore, shal not lacke: he that deſpiſeth him that asketh, shal ſuſteyne penurie. <na>[1]</na>
When the impious shal riſe, men shal be hid: when they shal perish, the iuſt shal be multiplied. <na>[1]</na>
THE man, that with ſtiffe necke contemneth him that rebuketh, ſoden deſtruction shal come vpon him: and health shal not folow him. <na>[1]</na>
In the multiplication of iuſt men, the common people shal reioyce: when the impious shal take princedom, the people shal mourne. <na>[1]</na>
A man that loueth wiſedom, maketh his father glad: but he that maintaineth harlots, shal deſtroy his ſubſtance. <na>[1]</na>
A iuſt king ſetteth vp the land, a couetous man shal deſtroy it. <na>[1]</na>
A man, that with fayre, and fayned wordes ſpeaketh to his frend, ſpreadeth a nette to his ſteppes. <na>[1]</na>
A ſnare shal intangle the wicked man ſinning: and the iuſt shal praiſe and reioyce. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Iuſt ioy of the wickeds fal.

verses.text: The iuſt knoweth the cauſe of the poore: the impious is ignorant of knowlege. <na>[1]</na>
Peſtilent men diſſipate a citie: but the wiſe turne away furie. <na>[1]</na>
A wiſe man, if he contend with a foole, whether he be angrie, or whether he laugh, shal not finde reſt. <na>[1]</na>
Men of bloud hate the ſimple: but iuſt men ſeeke his ſoule. <na>[1]</na>
A foole vttereth al his ſpirit: a wiſeman differreth, and reſerueth til afterward. <na>[1]</na>
A prince that gladly heareth wordes of lying, hath al his ſeruants impious. <na>[1]</na>
The pooreman and the creditour haue mette one an other: our Lord is illuminatour of both. <na>[1]</na>
The king, that iudgeth the poore in truth, his throne shal be replenished for euer. <na>[1]</na>
Rod and rebuke geueth wiſedom: but the childe, that is left to his owne wil, confoundeth his mother. <na>[1]</na>
In the multiplication of the impious, wickednes shal be multiplied, and the iuſt shal ſee the ruines of them. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: God neuer permitteth al to be euil.

verses.text: Nurter thy ſonne, and he shal refresh thee, and shal geue delightes to thy ſoule. <na>[1]</na>
When prophecie shal fayle, the people shal be diſſipated: but he that keepeth the Law, is bleſſed. <na>[1]</na>
A ſeruant can not be taught by wordes: becauſe he vnderſtandeth that which thou ſayſt, and contemneth to anſwer. <na>[1]</na>
Haſt thou ſeene a man ſwifte to ſpeake? follie is rather to be hoped, then his amendement. <na>[1]</na>
He that nourisheth his ſeruant delicatly from his childhood, afterward shal feele him ſtubburne. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Subdue the flesh to the ſpirite.

verses.text: An angrie man prouoketh brawles: and he that is eaſie to indignation, shal be more prone to ſinne. <na>[1]</na>
Humiliation foloweth the proude: and glorie shal receiue the humble of ſpirite. <na>[1]</na>
He that is partaker with a theefe, hateth his owne ſoule: he heareth one adiuring, and telleth not. <na>[1]</na>
He that feareth man, shal ſoone fal: he that truſteth in our Lord shal be lifted vp. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Feare not men in God'ſ cauſe,

verses.text: Manie ſeeke after the face of the prince: & the iudgement of euerie one commeth forth from our Lord. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: remembering that God is Judge of all.

verses.text: The iuſt abhorre an impious man: & the impious abhorre them that are in the right way. <na>[1]</na> The ſonne that keepeth the word, shal be out of perdition. <na>[2]</na>
THE wordes of the Gatherer the ſonne of Vomiter. The viſion, that the man ſpake, with whom God is, and who being ſtrengthened by God abiding with him, ſayd:
I am <na>(a)</na> moſt foolish of men, & the wiſedom of men is not with me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The wiſeſt man beſt knoweth that he wanteth much of perfect wiſdom yet in his humilitie ſuppoſeth, that others haue attained ſome what more then himſelf.

verses.text: I haue not learned wiſedom, and haue not knowen the ſcience of ſaints.

<na>(b)</na> Who hath aſcended into heauen and deſcended? who hath conteyned the ſpirit in his handes? who hath bound the waters together as in a garment? who hath rayſed vp al the borders of the earth? what is his name, and what is the name of his ſonne, if thou know?

notes.label: b
notes.text: Chriſt the Sonne of God is wiſdom it ſelf, and as the Sonne of man hath perfect wiſdom.

verses.text: Euerie word of God tryed by fyre, is a buckler to them that hope in him:
Adde not any thing to his wordes, and ſo thou be reproued and found a lyer:
Two thinges I haue asked thee, denie them not to me before I dye.
Vanitie, and lying wordes make far from me. Beggerie, and riches geue me not: geue only things neceſſarie for my ſuſtenance:
leſt perhaps being filled I be allured to denie, and may ſay: Who is the Lord? or being compelled by pouertie I may ſteale, and forſweare the name of my God.
<na>(c)</na> Accuſe not a ſeruant to his maſter, leſt perhaps he curſe thee, and thou fal.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Bondſlaues are to be pitied, and not affliction added to the afflicted.

verses.text: There is <na>(d)</na> a generation that curſeth their father, and that bleſſeth not their mother.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Foure execrable vices. Ingratitude. Hypocriſie: Inſolencie: Oppreſſion of the poore.

verses.text: A generation, that ſemeth to it ſelf cleane, & yet is not washed from their filthines.
A generation, whoſe eies are loftie, and the eielids therof ſet vp on high.
A generation, that for teeth hath ſwordes, and chaweth with theyr grinding teeth, that they may eate the needie out of the earth, and the poore from among men.
The horseleach hath <na>(e)</na> two daughters that ſay: Bring, bring. Three things are vnſatiable, the fourth neuer ſayth it ſufficeth.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Concupiſcence of the flesh, & of the eyes. · Enuie, Luxurie, Auarice, & Ambition.

verses.text: Hel, and the mouth of the matrice, & the earth which is not ſatisfied with water: but the fyre neuer ſayth it ſufficeth.
The eie, that <na>(f)</na> ſcorneth his father, & that deſpiſeth the trauail of his mother, in bearing him, let the rauens of the torrents pick it out, and the young of the eagle eate it.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Dishonour of parents shal be ſeuerely punished.

verses.text: Three thinges are hard to me, and of the fourth I am vtterly ignorant.
The way of an eagle in the ayre, the way of a ſerpent vpon a rocke, the way of a shippe in the middes of the ſea, and <na>(g)</na> the way of a man in youth.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Yong men folowing carnal appetite, can no more geue account of their actions, then of the vvayes vvhich an eagle, a ſerpent, and a shippe haue paſſed.

verses.text: Such is alſo the way of an adulterous woman, which eateth, and wyping her mouth ſayth: I haue done no euil.
By three thinges the earth is moued, and the fourth it can not ſuſteyne.
By a ſeruant when he shal reigne: by a foole when he shal be filled with meate:
by an odious woman when she shal be taken in matrimonie: & by a bondwoman when she shal be heyre to her miſtreſſe.
There are <na>(h)</na> foure the leaſt thinges of the earth, and they are wiſer then the wiſe.

notes.label: h
notes.text: By theſe examples are commended foure vertues, Induſtrie, Prudence, Concord, and Humilitie.

verses.text: The antes, a weake people, which prepareth in the harueſt meate for themſelues:
The leueret, a people not ſtrong, which placeth his bed in the rocke:
The locuſt hath no king, and they go out al by their troopes:
The ſtellion ſtayeth on his handes, & tarieth in kings houſes.
<na>(i)</na> There are three thinges which go wel, and the fourth that goeth happely.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Other foure Fortitude, Chaſtitie, Order, and Iuſtice.

verses.text: The lyon, the ſtrongeſt of beaſtes shal feare at the meeting of none:
the cocke gyrded about the loines, and the ramme: alſo the king, againſt whom none can reſiſt.
There is that <na>(k)</na> hath appeared a foole after that he was lifted vp on high: for if he had vnderſtood, he would haue layd his hand vpon his mouth.

And he that <na>(l)</na> ſtrongly preſſeth the pappes to wring out milke, ſtrayneth out butter, and he that violently cleanceth his noſe, wringeth out bloud: & he that prouoketh angers, bringeth forth diſcordes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Moderation is neceſſarie in al actions.

chapters.summary: A right wiſeman thinketh humbly of himſelf. 4. knowing that Gods workes are inſcrutable, and perfect: 8. deſireth truth in al thinges, & mediocritie in riches. 11. Abhorreth certaine ſortes of men, 15. & certaine execrable thinges 18. noteth certaine things hard to be knowen: 21. other thinges intolerable: 24. others admirable. 32. the tongue dangerous. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: The fourth part. Other ſingular precepts, with praiſe of a prudent woman.

verses.text: THE <na>(a)</na> wordes of Lamuel the king. The viſion wherwith his mother inſtructed him.

notes.label: a
notes.text: Wordes perteining to Salomon, ſpoken to him by his mother: who here calleth him Lamuel, ſignifying, God with him.

verses.text: What ô my beloued, what ô the beloued of my wombe, what ô beloued of my vowes?
Geue not thy ſubſtance to wemen, & thy riches to deſtroy kinges.
Geue not to kinges, ô Lamuel, geue not wine to kinges: becauſe there is no ſecrete where drunknes reigneth,
& leſt perhaps they drinke, & forget iudgements, & change the cauſe of the children of the poore.
Geue ſtrong drinke to them that be ſad, and wine vnto them, that are of a penſiue minde:
let them drinke, and forget their pouertie, and not remember their ſorow any more.
Open thy mouth to <na>(b)</na> the dumme, & to the cauſe of al the children that paſſe:

notes.label: b
notes.text: Doctrine is moſt profitable to thoſe, that are modeſtly dumme, more vvilling to heare then to ſpeake.

verses.text: open thy mouth, <na>(c)</na> decree that which is iuſt, & iudge the needie & poore.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The chief & moſt proper office of a king is to do iuſtice.

verses.text: A valiant woman <na>(d)</na> who shal finde? far, and from the vtmoſt borders is the price of her.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A woman of ſuch perfectió as is here deſcribed, is in dede rare, yet poſſible to be found.

verses.text: The hart of her husband truſteth in her, and he shal not neede ſpoyles.
She shal render good, and not euil, al the dayes of her life.
She hath ſought wool and flaxe, and hath wrought by the counſel of her handes.
She is become as a marchants shippe, bringing her bread from farre.
And she hath riſen in the night, and geuen pray to her houshold, and meates to her handmaides.
She hath vewed a filde, and bought it, of the fruite of her handes she hath planted a vineyard.
She hath gyrded her loines with ſtrength, and hath ſtrengthened her arme.
She hath taſted, and ſene that her traficke is good: her lampe shal not be extinguished in the night.
She hath put her hand to ſtrong thinges, and her fingers haue taken hold of <na>(e)</na> the ſpindle.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Flaxe on the diſtaffe ſignifieth purpoſe to do good workes, yarne on the ſpindle the vvorke vvel begune, which geueth confidence in God that the ſame shal be perfect and haue due revvard.

verses.text: She hath opened her hand to the needie, and ſtretched out her palmes to the poore.
She shal not feare for her houſe in the coldes of ſnow: for al her houshould are clothed with duble.
Tapeſtrie clothing she hath made to herſelf: ſilke, and purple is her garment.
Her husband is noble in the gates, when he shal ſitte with the ſenatours of the land.
She <na>(f)</na> made ſindon, and ſold it, and deliuered a girdle to the Chananeite.

notes.label: f
notes.text: They make and ſel cloth, which lerning and obſeruing Gods lavv, do teach it others.

verses.text: Strength and beautie is her garment, and she shal laugh in the later day.
She hath opened her mouth to wiſedom, and the law of clemencie is in her tongue.
She hath conſidered the pathes of her houſe, and hath not eaten her bread idle.
Her children aroſe, and commended her to be moſt bleſſed: her husband, and he prayſed her.
Manie daughters haue gathered together riches: thou haſt paſſed them al.
<na>(g)</na> Grace is deceitful, and beautie is vayne: the woman that feareth our Lord shal be prayſed.

notes.label: g
notes.text: External comelines is not durable: but the feare of God is more vvorthie of praiſe.

verses.text: Geue ye to her <na>(h)</na> of the fruite of her handes: and let her workes praiſe her <na>(i)</na> in the gates.

notes.label: i
notes.text: at the tribunal ſeate of iudgement.

chapters.summary: An exhortation to chaſtitie, temperance, 8. and to workes of mercie. 10. with praiſe of a valiant wiſe woman.
